7.8 The Spectrum of Atomic Hydrogen in an External Magnetic Field Is Accounted for by the Zeeman Effect

We predicted at that time that the 2p→1s2p \rightarrow 1s2p→1s transition should be split into three lines, which is not in accord with experiment. In fact, ten lines are
observed. We claimed that this discrepancy is due to the spin of the electron, and in this section, we shall see how these ten lines arise.

The total magnetic moment is mL+mS\boldsymbol m_L+\boldsymbol m_SmL​+mS​, and the energy of its interaction
with an external magnetic field (which is taken to be in the z direction) is given by:

V=∣e∣Bz2me(Lz+gSz)V=\frac {|e|B_z}{2m_e}(L_z+gS_z)V=2me​∣e∣Bz​​(Lz​+gSz​)

For typical magnetic field strengths, the effect of VVV is small and can be treated by perturbation theory. The final result is that the states are split by:

ΔEmag=g(j,l)βBmjBz\Delta E_{mag}=g(j,l)\beta_Bm_jB_zΔEmag​=g(j,l)βB​mj​Bz​

where mj=−j,−j+1,⋯ ,0,1,⋯ ,+jm_j=-j,-j+1,\cdots,0,1,\cdots,+jmj​=−j,−j+1,⋯,0,1,⋯,+j and:

g(j,l)={2(l+12l+1)j=l+122l2l+1j=l−12g(j,l)=\left\{\begin{aligned} 2\left(\frac {l+1}{2l+1}\right) \quad j=l+\frac 12 \\[3mm] \frac {2l}{2l+1} \quad j=l-\frac 12 \end{aligned}\right.g(j,l)=⎩⎪⎪⎪⎨⎪⎪⎪⎧​2(2l+1l+1​)j=l+21​2l+12l​j=l−21​​

This quantity g(j,l)g(j,l)g(j,l) is known as the L****andé g factor. Note that g=2g=2g=2 for the 1s 2S1/21s\ ^2S_{1/2}1s 2S1/2​ states, 2/32/32/3 for the 2p 2P1/22p\ ^2P_{1/2}2p 2P1/2​ states, and 4/34/34/3 for the 2p 2P3/22p\ ^2P_{3/2}2p 2P3/2​ states.

Figure 7.13 shows the splitting of the 1s 2S1/21s\ ^2S_{1/2}1s 2S1/2​, 2p 2P1/22p\ ^2P_{1/2}2p 2P1/2​ and 2p 2P3/22p\ ^2P_{3/2}2p 2P3/2​ states in an external magnetic field. The allowed transitions (Δmj=0,±1\Delta m_j=0,\pm1Δmj​=0,±1) are indicated, along with a schematic sketch of the resulting spectrum. Note that there are ten lines in the 2p→1s2p \rightarrow 1s2p→1s transition.

（ 在考虑了自旋-轨道耦合之后，谱线进一步分裂，满足选律的能级跃迁所产生的谱线共有10条。 ）

7.9 The Schrödinger Equation for a Helium Atom Cannot Be Solved Exactly

The next system to study is the helium atom, whose Schrödinger equation is:

(−ℏ22M∇2−ℏ22me∇12−ℏ22me∇22)ψ(R,r1,r2)+(−2e24πϵ0∣R−r1∣−2e24πϵ0∣R−r2∣+e24πϵ0∣r1−r2∣)ψ(R,r1,r2)=Eψ(R,r1,r2)\left(-\frac {\hbar^2}{2M}\nabla^2-\frac {\hbar^2}{2m_e}\nabla_1^2-\frac {\hbar^2}{2m_e}\nabla_2^2 \right)\psi(\boldsymbol R,\boldsymbol r_1,\boldsymbol r_2)+\left(-\frac {2e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0|\boldsymbol R-\boldsymbol r_1|}-\frac {2e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0|\boldsymbol R-\boldsymbol r_2|}+\frac {e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0|\boldsymbol r_1-\boldsymbol r_2|} \right)\psi(\boldsymbol R,\boldsymbol r_1,\boldsymbol r_2)=E\psi(\boldsymbol R,\boldsymbol r_1,\boldsymbol r_2)(−2Mℏ2​∇2−2me​ℏ2​∇12​−2me​ℏ2​∇22​)ψ(R,r1​,r2​)+(−4πϵ0​∣R−r1​∣2e2​−4πϵ0​∣R−r2​∣2e2​+4πϵ0​∣r1​−r2​∣e2​)ψ(R,r1​,r2​)=Eψ(R,r1​,r2​)

In this equation, R\boldsymbol RR is the position of the helium nucleus, and r1\boldsymbol r_1r1​ and r2\boldsymbol r_2r2​ are the positions of the two electrons; MMM is the mass of the nucleus, and mem_eme​ is the electronic mass; ∇2\nabla^2∇2 is the Laplacian operator with respect to the position of the nucleus, and ∇12\nabla_1^2∇12​ and ∇22\nabla_2^2∇22​ are the Laplacian operators with respect to the positions of the electronic coordinates.

Realize that this is a three-body problem and not a two-body problem, and so the separation into center-of-mass and relative coordinates is much more complicated than it is for hydrogen.

Because M≫meM \gg m_eM≫me​, however, regarding the nucleus as fixed relative to the
motion of the electrons is still an excellent approximation:

−ℏ22me(∇12+∇22)ψ(r1,r2)−2e24πϵ0(1r1+1r2)ψ(r1,r2)+e24πϵ0∣r1−r2∣ψ(r1,r2)=Eψ(r1,r2)-\frac {\hbar^2}{2m_e}\left(\nabla^2_1+\nabla_2^2\right)\psi(\boldsymbol r_1,\boldsymbol r_2) - \frac {2e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\left(\frac 1{r_1}+\frac 1{r_2} \right)\psi(\boldsymbol r_1,\boldsymbol r_2) + \frac {e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0|\boldsymbol r_1 - \boldsymbol r_2|}\psi(\boldsymbol r_1,\boldsymbol r_2)=E\psi(\boldsymbol r_1,\boldsymbol r_2)−2me​ℏ2​(∇12​+∇22​)ψ(r1​,r2​)−4πϵ0​2e2​(r1​1​+r2​1​)ψ(r1​,r2​)+4πϵ0​∣r1​−r2​∣e2​ψ(r1​,r2​)=Eψ(r1​,r2​)

Even this simplified equation cannot be solved exactly.

Because we cannot solve the equation exactly, we must resort to some approximation method. Fortunately, two quite different approximation methods that can yield extremely good results have found wide use in quantum chemistry. These are called the variational method and perturbation theory and are presented in the next chapter.

总结

本章的内容可以说是结构化学/量子化学老生常谈的部分了，很多结论在无机化学中也都很熟悉，另外还涉及了一些光谱学的内容。

entry.title: 《Quantum Chemistry》章末总结6
entry.content:
第六章是刚性转子和转动光谱。

Chapter 6 The Rigid Rotator and Rotational Spectroscopy

The rotation of a diatomic molecule can be described by a rigid rotator, which is like a rotating dumbbell. Using the concept of a reduced mass, we can picture the rotator as a body of reduced mass μ\muμ rotating about a fixed center.

This problem lends itself naturally to spherical coordinates, and the wave functions are functions of θ\thetaθ and ϕ\phiϕ, the two angles in spherical coordinates. The wave functions are called spherical harmonics and occur in many problems involving a fixed center.

Solving the Schrödinger equation for a rigid rotator is a fairly lengthy process, and so in most of this chapter we shall simply present and discuss the energies and the corresponding wave functions.

（ 描述转动问题会很自然地引入球坐标系，后面在解氢原子时也是在球坐标系下进行的。 ）

6.1 The Energy Levels of a Rigid Rotator Are E=ℏ2J(J+1)/2IE=\hbar^2J(J+1)/2IE=ℏ2J(J+1)/2I

In this section, we will discuss a simple model for a rotating diatomic molecule. The model consists of two point masses m1m_1m1​ and m2m_2m2​ at fixed distances l1l_1l1​ and l2l_2l2​ from their center of mass (cf. Figure 6.1).

Because the distance between the two masses is fixed, this model is referred to as the rigid-rotator model. Even though a diatomic molecule
vibrates as it rotates, the vibrational amplitude is small compared with the bond length, so considering the bond length fixed is a good approximation.

（ 对于双原子分子，在考虑转动时，可以忽略振动对于键长的微小影响，即把双原子分子当成刚性转子处理。 ）

Let the molecule rotate about its center of mass at a frequency of νrot\nu_{rot}νrot​ cycles per second. The kinetic energy of the rigid rotator is:

T=12m1v12+12m2v22=12(m1l12+m2l22)ω2=12Iω2\begin{aligned} T &=\frac 12m_1v_1^2+\frac 12m_2v_2^2=\frac 12(m_1l_1^2+m_2l_2^2)\omega^2 \\[3mm] &= \frac 12I\omega^2 \end{aligned}T​=21​m1​v12​+21​m2​v22​=21​(m1​l12​+m2​l22​)ω2=21​Iω2​

where III, the moment of inertia, is given by:

I=m1l12+m2l22=μl2I=m_1l_1^2+m_2l_2^2=\mu l^2I=m1​l12​+m2​l22​=μl2

where l=l1+l2l=l_1+l_2l=l1​+l2​ and μ\muμ is the reduced mass. We may consider the equation to be an equation for the moment of inertia of a single body of mass μ\muμ rotating at a distance lll from a fixed center. Thus, we have transformed a two-body problem into an equivalent one-body problem.

The angular momentum LLL is:

L=IωL=I\omegaL=Iω

and the kinetic energy is:

T=L22IT=\frac {L^2}{2I}T=2IL2​

There is no potential energy term because in the absence of any external forces the energy of the molecule does not depend on its orientation in space. The Hamiltonian operator of a rigid rotator is therefore just the kinetic energy operator:

H^=T^=−ℏ22μ∇2(r constant)\hat H=\hat T=-\frac {\hbar^2}{2\mu}\nabla^2 \quad (r\ constant)H^=T^=−2μℏ2​∇2(r constant)

We need to convert ∇2\nabla^2∇2 from cartesian coordinates to spherical coordinates:

∇2=1r2∂∂r(r2∂∂r)θ,ϕ+1r2sin⁡θ∂∂θ(sin⁡θ∂∂θ)r,ϕ+1r2sin⁡2θ(∂2∂ϕ2)r,θ\nabla^2=\frac 1{r^2}\frac {\partial}{\partial r} \left( r^2\frac {\partial}{\partial r}\right)_{\theta,\phi}+\frac 1{r^2\sin\theta}\frac {\partial}{\partial \theta} \left(\sin\theta\frac {\partial}{\partial \theta} \right)_{r,\phi}+\frac 1{r^2\sin^2\theta} \left(\frac {\partial^2}{\partial\phi^2} \right)_{r,\theta}∇2=r21​∂r∂​(r2∂r∂​)θ,ϕ​+r2sinθ1​∂θ∂​(sinθ∂θ∂​)r,ϕ​+r2sin2θ1​(∂ϕ2∂2​)r,θ​

The rigid rotator is a special case where rrr is equal to a constant, lll, so it becomes:

∇2=1l2sin⁡θ∂∂θ(sin⁡θ∂∂θ)+1l2sin⁡2θ∂2∂ϕ2(r constant)\nabla^2=\frac 1{l^2\sin\theta}\frac {\partial}{\partial \theta} \left(\sin\theta\frac {\partial}{\partial \theta} \right)+\frac 1{l^2\sin^2\theta} \frac {\partial^2}{\partial\phi^2} \quad (r\ constant)∇2=l2sinθ1​∂θ∂​(sinθ∂θ∂​)+l2sin2θ1​∂ϕ2∂2​(r constant)

And now we obtain:

H^=−ℏ22I[1sin⁡θ∂∂θ(sin⁡θ∂∂θ)+1sin⁡2θ(∂2∂ϕ2)]\hat H=-\frac {\hbar^2}{2I} \left[\frac {1}{\sin\theta}\frac {\partial}{\partial \theta} \left(\sin\theta \frac {\partial}{\partial \theta} \right)+\frac 1{\sin^2\theta} \left(\frac {\partial^2}{\partial \phi^2} \right) \right]H^=−2Iℏ2​[sinθ1​∂θ∂​(sinθ∂θ∂​)+sin2θ1​(∂ϕ2∂2​)]

L^2=−ℏ2[1sin⁡θ∂∂θ(sin⁡θ∂∂θ)+1sin⁡2θ(∂2∂ϕ2)]\hat L^2=-\hbar^2 \left[\frac {1}{\sin\theta}\frac {\partial}{\partial \theta} \left(\sin\theta \frac {\partial}{\partial \theta} \right)+\frac 1{\sin^2\theta} \left(\frac {\partial^2}{\partial \phi^2} \right) \right]L^2=−ℏ2[sinθ1​∂θ∂​(sinθ∂θ∂​)+sin2θ1​(∂ϕ2∂2​)]

The orientation of a rigid rotator is completely specified by the two angles θ\thetaθ and ϕ\phiϕ, so rigid-rotator wave functions depend upon only these two variables. So the Schrödinger equation for a rigid rotator reads:

H^Y(θ,ϕ)=EY(θ,ϕ)\hat H Y(\theta,\phi)=EY(\theta,\phi)H^Y(θ,ϕ)=EY(θ,ϕ)

To solve the equation, we again use the method of separation of variables:

Y(θ,ϕ)=Θ(θ)Φ(ϕ)Y(\theta,\phi)=\Theta(\theta)\Phi(\phi)Y(θ,ϕ)=Θ(θ)Φ(ϕ)

We find:

sin⁡θΘ(θ)ddθ(sin⁡θdΘdθ)+βsin⁡2θ+1Φ(ϕ)d2Φdϕ2=0(β=2IEℏ2)\frac {\sin\theta}{\Theta(\theta)}\frac {d}{d\theta} \left(\sin\theta\frac {d\Theta}{d\theta} \right)+\beta \sin^2\theta+\frac 1{\Phi(\phi)}\frac {d^2\Phi}{d\phi^2}=0 \quad \left(\beta=\frac {2IE}{\hbar^2} \right)Θ(θ)sinθ​dθd​(sinθdθdΘ​)+βsin2θ+Φ(ϕ)1​dϕ2d2Φ​=0(β=ℏ22IE​)

Because θ\thetaθ and ϕ\phiϕ are independent variables, we must have:

sin⁡θΘ(θ)ddθ(sin⁡θdΘdθ)+βsin⁡2θ=m2\frac {\sin\theta}{\Theta(\theta)}\frac {d}{d\theta} \left(\sin\theta\frac {d\Theta}{d\theta} \right)+\beta \sin^2\theta = m^2Θ(θ)sinθ​dθd​(sinθdθdΘ​)+βsin2θ=m2

and:

1Φ(ϕ)d2Φdϕ2=−m2\frac 1{\Phi(\phi)}\frac {d^2\Phi}{d\phi^2} = -m^2Φ(ϕ)1​dϕ2d2Φ​=−m2

where m2m^2m2 is a constant.

The second equation contains only constant coefficients, it is relatively easy to solve:

Φ(ϕ)=AmeimϕandΦ(ϕ)=A−me−imϕ\Phi(\phi)=A_me^{im\phi} \quad and \quad \Phi(\phi)=A_{-m}e^{-im\phi}Φ(ϕ)=Am​eimϕandΦ(ϕ)=A−m​e−imϕ

The requirement that Φ(ϕ)\Phi(\phi)Φ(ϕ) be a single-valued function of ϕ\phiϕ is:

Φ(ϕ+2π)=Φ(ϕ)\Phi(\phi+2\pi)=\Phi(\phi)Φ(ϕ+2π)=Φ(ϕ)

With this, we obtain:

cos⁡(2πm)±isin⁡(2πm)=1\cos(2\pi m)\pm i \sin(2\pi m)=1cos(2πm)±isin(2πm)=1

which implies that m=0,±1,±2,⋯m=0,\pm1,\pm2,\cdotsm=0,±1,±2,⋯. And:

Φm(ϕ)=Ameimϕm=0,±1,±2,⋯\Phi_m(\phi)=A_me^{im\phi} \quad m=0,\pm1,\pm2,\cdotsΦm​(ϕ)=Am​eimϕm=0,±1,±2,⋯

We can find the value of AmA_mAm​ by requiring that the Φm(ϕ)\Phi_m(\phi)Φm​(ϕ) be normalized, Am=(2π)−1/2A_m=(2\pi)^{-1/2}Am​=(2π)−1/2.

（ 对于含Φ\PhiΦ的方程，易于给出它的解。根据函数单值性的要求，可以求得mmm的取值必须为整数。 ）

When we solve the first equation, it turns out naturally that β\betaβ must obey the condition:

β=J(J+1)J=0,1,2,⋯\beta=J(J+1) \quad J=0,1,2,\cdotsβ=J(J+1)J=0,1,2,⋯

It means:

EJ=ℏ22IJ(J+1)=BJ(J+1)J=0,1,2,⋯E_J=\frac {\hbar^2}{2I}J(J+1)=BJ(J+1) \quad J=0,1,2,\cdotsEJ​=2Iℏ2​J(J+1)=BJ(J+1)J=0,1,2,⋯

where B=ℏ2/2IB=\hbar^2/2IB=ℏ2/2I is called the rotational constant of the molecule.

Once again, we obtain a set of discrete energy levels. In addition to the allowed energies given by the equation, we also find that each energy level has a degeneracy gJg_JgJ​ given by:

gJ=2J+1g_J=2J+1gJ​=2J+1

We’ll see later that this degeneracy is due to the fact that mmm can take on the value −J-J−J through +J+J+J.

（ 含Θ\ThetaΘ的方程求解起来较为复杂，仍然是使用级数展开法，涉及到连带勒让德方程等，详细过程见相关量子力学教材。 ）

6.2 The Rigid Rotator Is a Model for a Rotating Diatomic Molecule

We will show in Section 6.7 that the selection rule for the rigid rotator says that transitions are allowed only from adjacent states or that:

ΔJ=±1\Delta J=\pm1ΔJ=±1

In addition to the requirement that ΔJ=±1\Delta J=\pm1ΔJ=±1, the molecule must also possess a permanent dipole moment to absorb electromagnetic radiation. Thus, HClHClHCl has a pure rotational spectrum, but N2N_2N2​ does not.

In the case of absorption of electromagnetic radiation, the energy difference is:

ΔE=EJ+1−EJ=ℏ22I[(J+1)(J+2)−J(J+1)]=ℏ2I(J+1)=h24π2I(J+1)J=0,1,2,⋯\begin{aligned} \Delta E &= E_{J+1}-E_J=\frac {\hbar^2}{2I}[(J+1)(J+2)-J(J+1)] \\[3mm] &=\frac {\hbar^2}{I}(J+1)=\frac {h^2}{4\pi^2I}(J+1) \quad J=0,1,2,\cdots \end{aligned}ΔE​=EJ+1​−EJ​=2Iℏ2​[(J+1)(J+2)−J(J+1)]=Iℏ2​(J+1)=4π2Ih2​(J+1)J=0,1,2,⋯​

Using the Bohr frequency condition ΔE=hνobs\Delta E=h\nu_{obs}ΔE=hνobs​ the frequencies at which the absorption transitions occur are:

νobs=h4π2I(J+1)J=0,1,2,⋯\nu_{obs}=\frac {h}{4\pi^2 I}(J+1) \quad J=0,1,2,\cdotsνobs​=4π2Ih​(J+1)J=0,1,2,⋯

The moment of inertia of a diatomic molecule typically ranges from 10−4510^{-45}10−45 to 10−46 kg⋅m210^{-46}\,kg\cdot m^210−46kg⋅m2. Substituting I=5×10−46 kg⋅m2I=5\times10^{-46}\,kg\cdot m^2I=5×10−46kg⋅m2 into the equation shows that the absorption frequencies are about 2×10102\times10^{10}2×1010 to 1011 Hz10^{11}\,Hz1011Hz. We see that these frequencies lie in the microwave region, and the study of rotational transitions in molecules is called microwave spectroscopy.

It is common practice in microwave spectroscopy to write the equation as:

νobs=2B(J+1)J=0,1,2,⋯\nu_{obs}=2B(J+1) \quad J=0,1,2,\cdotsνobs​=2B(J+1)J=0,1,2,⋯

where:

B=h8π2I (Hz)B=\frac h{8\pi^2I}\ (Hz)B=8π2Ih​ (Hz)

is the rotational constant expressed in units of hertz.

Furthermore, the transition frequency is commonly expessed in terms of wave numbers rather than hertz:

ω~obs=2B~(J+1)J=0,1,2,⋯\tilde\omega_{obs}=2\tilde B(J+1) \quad J=0,1,2,\cdotsω~obs​=2B~(J+1)J=0,1,2,⋯

where B~\tilde BB~ is the rotational constant expressed in units of wave numbers:

B~=h8π2cI (cm−1)\tilde B=\frac h{8\pi^2cI}\ (cm^{-1})B~=8π2cIh​ (cm−1)

We see that the rigid-rotator model predicts that the microwave spectrum of a diatomic molecule consists of a series of equally spaced lines with a separation of 2B HZ2B\,HZ2BHZ or 2B~ cm−12\tilde B\,cm^{-1}2B~cm−1.

（ 刚性转子模型同样受到选律的限制，这意味着双原子分子转动光谱上的谱线都是等间距的。 ）

6.3 Rotational Transitions Accompany Vibrational Transitions

In the previous chapter, we showed that the vibrational motion of a diatomic molecule can be well approximated by a ha1monic oscillator, and in this chapter, we have just seen that the rotational motion of a diatomic molecule can be well represented by a rigid rotator. We combine these ideas and say that the rotational-vibrational motion of a diatomic molecule can be well approximated by the rigid rotator- harmonic oscillator model.

Within the rigid rotator-harmonic oscillator approximation, the rotational and vibrational energy of a diatomic molecule is given by:

Ev,J=(v+12)hν+BJ(J+1)E_{v,J}= \left(v+\frac 12 \right)h\nu+BJ(J+1)Ev,J​=(v+21​)hν+BJ(J+1)

or:

E~v,J=(v+12)ω~+B~J(J+1)v,J=0,1,2,⋯\tilde E_{v,J}= \left(v+\frac 12 \right)\tilde \omega + \tilde BJ(J+1) \quad v,J=0,1,2,\cdotsE~v,J​=(v+21​)ω~+B~J(J+1)v,J=0,1,2,⋯

Typical values of ω~\tilde \omegaω~ and B~\tilde BB~ are of the order of 103 cm−110^3\,cm^{-1}103cm−1 and 1 cm−11\,cm^{-1}1cm−1, respectively, so the spacing between vibrational energy levels is about 100 to 1000 times the spacing between rotational levels.

When a molecule absorbs infrared radiation, the vibrational transition is accompanied by a rotational transition. The rotation-vibration spectrum of HBr(g)HBr(g)HBr(g) is shown in Figure 6.4.

The gap centered around 2560 cm−12560\,cm^{-1}2560cm−1 corresponds to the missing line at ω~\tilde \omegaω~, because the transition ΔJ=0\Delta J=0ΔJ=0 is forbidden. On each side of the gap is a series of lines whose spacing is about 10 cm−110\,cm^{-1}10cm−1. The series toward the high-frequency side is called the R branch and is due to rotational transitions with ΔJ=+1\Delta J=+1ΔJ=+1. The series toward the low frequencies is called the P branch and is due to rotational transitions with ΔJ=−1\Delta J=-1ΔJ=−1.

（ 可以从图中看出，振动光谱谱线的能差远大于转动光谱谱线的能差，也就是说在发生振动能级跃迁的同时一定伴随着转动能级跃迁。 ）

But we also see several features we cannot explain. Close examination shows that the lines in the R branch are more closely spaced with increasing frequency and that the lines of the P branch become further apart with decreasing frequency. We will discuss the spacing of the lines in the R and P branches in the next section.

6.4 Rotation-Vibration lnteraction Accounts for the Unequal Spacing of the Lines in the P and R Branches of a Rotation-Vibration Spectrum

The energies of a rigid rotator-harmonic oscillator are given by:

E~v,J=ω~(v+12)+B~J(J+1)\tilde E_{v,J}=\tilde \omega \left(v+\frac 12 \right)+\tilde BJ(J+1)E~v,J​=ω~(v+21​)+B~J(J+1)

where B~=h/8π2cI=h/8π2cμl2\tilde B=h/8\pi^2cI=h/8\pi^2c\mu l^2B~=h/8π2cI=h/8π2cμl2.

Because the vibrational amplitude increases with the vibrational state (cf. Figure 6.3), we expect that lll should increase slightly with vvv, causing B~\tilde BB~ to decrease with increasing vvv. We will indicate the dependence of B~\tilde BB~ upon vvv by using B~v\tilde B_vB~v​ in place of B~\tilde BB~:

E~v,J=ω~(v+12)+B~vJ(J+1)(B~v=B~e−α~e(v+12))\tilde E_{v,J}=\tilde \omega \left(v+\frac 12 \right)+\tilde B_vJ(J+1) \quad \left(\tilde B_v=\tilde B_e-\tilde \alpha_e \left(v+\frac 12 \right)\right)E~v,J​=ω~(v+21​)+B~v​J(J+1)(B~v​=B~e​−α~e​(v+21​))

The dependence of B~\tilde BB~ on vvv is called rotation-vibration interaction. If we consider a v=0→1v=0\rightarrow1v=0→1 transition, then the frequencies of the P and R branches will be given by:

ν~R(ΔJ=+1)=E1,J+1−E0,J=32ω~+B~1(J+1)(J+2)−12ω~−B~0J(J+1)=ω~+2B~1+(3B~1−B~0)J+(B~1−B~0)J2J=0,1,2,⋯\begin{aligned} \tilde\nu_R(\Delta J=+1) &=E_{1,J+1}-E_{0,J} \\[3mm] &=\frac 32\tilde \omega+\tilde B_1(J+1)(J+2)-\frac 12\tilde\omega-\tilde B_0J(J+1) \\[3mm] &= \tilde\omega+2\tilde B_1+(3\tilde B_1-\tilde B_0)J+(\tilde B_1-\tilde B_0)J^2 \quad J=0,1,2,\cdots \end{aligned}ν~R​(ΔJ=+1)​=E1,J+1​−E0,J​=23​ω~+B~1​(J+1)(J+2)−21​ω~−B~0​J(J+1)=ω~+2B~1​+(3B~1​−B~0​)J+(B~1​−B~0​)J2J=0,1,2,⋯​

and:

ν~P(ΔJ=−1)=E1,J−1−E0,J=ω~−(B~1+B~0)J+(B~1−B~0)J2J=1,2,3,⋯\begin{aligned} \tilde\nu_P(\Delta J=-1) &=E_{1,J-1}-E_{0,J} \\[3mm] &= \tilde\omega-(\tilde B_1+\tilde B_0)J+(\tilde B_1-\tilde B_0)J^2 \quad J=1,2,3,\cdots \end{aligned}ν~P​(ΔJ=−1)​=E1,J−1​−E0,J​=ω~−(B~1​+B~0​)J+(B~1​−B~0​)J2J=1,2,3,⋯​

Because the bond length increases with increasing vvv, B~1<B~0\tilde B_1<\tilde B_0B~1​<B~0​, and therefore the spacing between the lines in the R branch decreases and the spacing between the lines in the P branch increases with increasing JJJ.

（ 由于振转相互作用的存在，振转光谱的P支谱线随波数减小，间隔实际上逐渐变大；R支谱线随波数增大，间隔实际上逐渐变小。 ）

6.5 The Lines in a Pure Rotational Spectrum Are Not Equally Spaced

We can find the line in a pure rotational spectrum aren’t exactly equally spaced as the rigid-rotator approximation predicts. The discrepancy can be resolved by realizing that a chemical bond is not truly rigid. As the molecule rotates more energetically (increasing JJJ), the centrifugal force causes the bond to stretch slightly.

This small effect can be treated by perturbation theory (Chapter 8), and the end result is that the energy can be written as:

EJ=B~J(J+1)−D~J2(J+1)2E_J=\tilde BJ(J+1)-\tilde DJ^2(J+1)^2EJ​=B~J(J+1)−D~J2(J+1)2

where D~\tilde DD~ is called the centrifugal distortion constant.

（ 高转动能级时，分子转动加剧，离心运动会使得化学键被拉长，我们引入离心畸变常数来描述离心对能量的影响。这意味着纯转动光谱也不是像刚性转子模型所显示的等间距光谱线。 ）

The frequencies of the absorption due to J→J+1J \rightarrow J+1J→J+1 transitions are given by:

ω~=EJ+1−EJ=2B~(J+1)−4D~(J+1)2J=0,1,2,⋯\begin{aligned} \tilde \omega &=E_{J+1}-E_J \\[3mm] &=2\tilde B(J+1)-4\tilde D(J+1)^2 \quad J=0,1,2,\cdots \end{aligned}ω~​=EJ+1​−EJ​=2B~(J+1)−4D~(J+1)2J=0,1,2,⋯​

The rotational enegy level of a rigid rotator (left) and a nonrigid rotator (right).

6.6 The Wave Functions of a Rigid Rotator Are Called Spherical Harmonics

We can get the normalized solution to the rigid-rortator wave functions:

YJm(θ,ϕ)=im+∣m∣[(2J+1)4π(J−∣m∣)!(J+∣m∣)!]1/2PJ∣m∣(cos⁡θ)eimϕY_J^m(\theta,\phi)=i^{m+|m|} \left[\frac {(2J+1)}{4\pi}\frac {(J-|m|)!}{(J+|m|)!} \right]^{1/2} P_J^{|m|}(\cos\theta)e^{im\phi}YJm​(θ,ϕ)=im+∣m∣[4π(2J+1)​(J+∣m∣)!(J−∣m∣)!​]1/2PJ∣m∣​(cosθ)eimϕ

With J=0,1,2,⋯J=0,1,2,\cdotsJ=0,1,2,⋯ and m=0,±1,±2,⋯ ,±Jm=0,\pm1,\pm2,\cdots,\pm Jm=0,±1,±2,⋯,±J. They are also the angular part of the hydrogen atomic orbitals, are given by Θjm(θ)Φm(ϕ)\Theta_j^m(\theta)\Phi_m(\phi)Θjm​(θ)Φm​(ϕ).

（ 解方程的过程较为复杂，在此忽略，具体可参考量子力学教材。 ）

The YJm(θ,ϕ)Y_J^m(\theta,\phi)YJm​(θ,ϕ) form an orthonormal set:

∫0πdθsin⁡θ∫02πdϕYKm(θ,ϕ)∗YJ′k(θ,ϕ)=δJJ′δmk\int_0^{\pi}d\theta \sin\theta \int_0^{2\pi}d\phi Y_K^m(\theta,\phi)^*Y_{J'}^k(\theta,\phi)=\delta_{JJ'}\delta_{mk}∫0π​dθsinθ∫02π​dϕYKm​(θ,ϕ)∗YJ′k​(θ,ϕ)=δJJ′​δmk​

Note that the YJm(θ,ϕ)Y_J^m(\theta,\phi)YJm​(θ,ϕ) are orthonormal with respect to sin⁡θdθdϕ\sin\theta d\theta d\phisinθdθdϕ and not just dθdϕd\theta d\phidθdϕ. sin⁡θdθdϕ\sin\theta d\theta d\phisinθdθdϕ is an area element on the surface of a sphere of unit radius. So the YJm(θ,ϕ)Y_J^m(\theta,\phi)YJm​(θ,ϕ) are orthonormal over a spherical surface and so called spherical hramonics.

In summary, the Schrödinger equation for a rigid rotator is:

H^YJm(θ,ϕ)=ℏ2J(J+1)2IYJm(θ,ϕ)J=0,1,2,⋯\hat HY_J^m(\theta,\phi)=\frac {\hbar^2J(J+1)}{2I}Y_J^m(\theta,\phi) \quad J=0,1,2,\cdotsH^YJm​(θ,ϕ)=2Iℏ2J(J+1)​YJm​(θ,ϕ)J=0,1,2,⋯

Because H^=L^2/2I\hat H=\hat L^2/2IH^=L^2/2I, we can write the expression of L^2\hat L^2L^2 and the eigenvalue equation for L^2\hat L^2L^2 is:

L^2YJm(θ,ϕ)=ℏ2J(J+1)YJm(θ,ϕ)\hat L^2Y_J^m(\theta,\phi)=\hbar^2J(J+1)Y_J^m(\theta,\phi)L^2YJm​(θ,ϕ)=ℏ2J(J+1)YJm​(θ,ϕ)

Thus, we see that the spherical harmonics are also eigenfunctions of L^2\hat L^2L^2 and that the square of the angular momentum can have only the values given by:

L2=ℏ2J(J+1)J=0,1,2,⋯L^2=\hbar^2J(J+1) \quad J=0,1,2,\cdotsL2=ℏ2J(J+1)J=0,1,2,⋯

We shall discuss angular momentum more fully in Section 6.8.

6.7 The Selection Rule in the Rigid-Rotator Approximation Is ΔJ=±1\Delta J=\pm1ΔJ=±1

As we said when we discussed the selection rule for a harmonic oscillator in Section 5.12, the probability that a molecule makes a transition from one vibrational state to another when it is irradiated with electromagnetic radiation in the z direction is given by the square of an integral of the form:

⟨v′∣μz∣v⟩=∫−∞∞dxψv′(x)μz(x)ψv(x)\langle v'|\mu_z|v \rangle =\int_{-\infin}^{\infin} dx\psi_{v'}(x)\mu_z(x)\psi_v(x)⟨v′∣μz​∣v⟩=∫−∞∞​dxψv′​(x)μz​(x)ψv​(x)

In the case of a rigid rotator, the transition dipole moment integral takes the form (we shall derive this result in Section 8.6):

⟨J′,m′∣μz∣J,m⟩=∫02π∫0πYJ′m′(θ,ϕ)∗μzYJm(θ,ϕ)sin⁡θdθdϕ\langle J',m'|\mu_z|J,m \rangle =\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\pi}Y_{J'}^{m'}(\theta,\phi)^*\mu_zY_J^m(\theta,\phi) \sin\theta d\theta d\phi⟨J′,m′∣μz​∣J,m⟩=∫02π​∫0π​YJ′m′​(θ,ϕ)∗μz​YJm​(θ,ϕ)sinθdθdϕ

Using the fact that μz=μ0cos⁡θ\mu_z=\mu_0 \cos\thetaμz​=μ0​cosθ gives:

⟨J′,m′∣μz∣J,m⟩=μ0∫02π∫0πYJ′m′(θ,ϕ)∗YJm(θ,ϕ)cos⁡θsin⁡θdθdϕ\langle J',m'|\mu_z|J,m \rangle =\mu_0\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\pi}Y_{J'}^{m'}(\theta,\phi)^*Y_J^m(\theta,\phi) \cos\theta \sin\theta d\theta d\phi⟨J′,m′∣μz​∣J,m⟩=μ0​∫02π​∫0π​YJ′m′​(θ,ϕ)∗YJm​(θ,ϕ)cosθsinθdθdϕ

Notice that μ0\mu_0μ0​ must be nonzero for the transition moment to be nonzero. Thus, we have now proven our earlier assertion that a molecule must have a permanent dipole moment for it to have a pure rotational spectrum.

Now we substitute the YJm(θ,ϕ)Y_J^m(\theta,\phi)YJm​(θ,ϕ) into the equation and let x=cos⁡θx=\cos\thetax=cosθ to obtain:

⟨J′,m′∣μz∣J,m⟩=μ0NJ′m′NJm∫02πdϕei(m−m′)ϕ∫−11dx xPJ′∣m′∣(x)PJ∣m∣(x)\langle J',m'|\mu_z|J,m \rangle =\mu_0N_{J'm'}N_{Jm} \int_0^{2\pi}d\phi e^{i(m-m')\phi} \int_{-1}^{1} dx\ x P_{J'}^{|m'|}(x) P_J^{|m|}(x)⟨J′,m′∣μz​∣J,m⟩=μ0​NJ′m′​NJm​∫02π​dϕei(m−m′)ϕ∫−11​dx xPJ′∣m′∣​(x)PJ∣m∣​(x)

The integral over ϕ\phiϕ is zero unless m=m′m=m'm=m′, so we find that Δm=0\Delta m=0Δm=0 is part of the rigid-rotator selection rule. Integration over ϕ\phiϕ for m=m′m=m'm=m′ gives a factor of 2π2\pi2π, so we have:

⟨J′,m′∣μz∣J,m⟩=2πμ0NJ′m′NJm∫−11dx xPJ′∣m′∣(x)PJ∣m∣(x)\langle J',m'|\mu_z|J,m \rangle =2\pi\mu_0N_{J'm'}N_{Jm} \int_{-1}^{1} dx\ x P_{J'}^{|m'|}(x) P_J^{|m|}(x)⟨J′,m′∣μz​∣J,m⟩=2πμ0​NJ′m′​NJm​∫−11​dx xPJ′∣m′∣​(x)PJ∣m∣​(x)

We can evaluate this integral in general by using the recursion formula:

(2J+1)xPJ∣m∣(x)=(J−∣m∣+1)PJ+1∣m∣(x)+(J+∣m∣)PJ−1∣m∣(x)(2J+1)xP_J^{|m|}(x)=(J-|m|+1)P_{J+1}^{|m|}(x)+(J+|m|)P_{J-1}^{|m|}(x)(2J+1)xPJ∣m∣​(x)=(J−∣m∣+1)PJ+1∣m∣​(x)+(J+∣m∣)PJ−1∣m∣​(x)

By using this relation, we obtain:

⟨J′,m∣μz∣J,m⟩=2πμ0NJ′mNJm∫−11dx PJ′∣m∣(x)×[(J−∣m∣+1)2J+1PJ+1∣m∣(x)+(J+∣m∣)2J+1PJ−1∣m∣(x)]\begin{aligned} \langle J',m|\mu_z|J,m \rangle= &2\pi\mu_0N_{J'm}N_{Jm}\int_{-1}^1dx\ P_{J'}^{|m|}(x) \\[3mm] &\times \left[\frac {(J-|m|+1)}{2J+1}P_{J+1}^{|m|}(x)+\frac {(J+|m|)}{2J+1}P_{J-1}^{|m|}(x) \right] \end{aligned}⟨J′,m∣μz​∣J,m⟩=​2πμ0​NJ′m​NJm​∫−11​dx PJ′∣m∣​(x)×[2J+1(J−∣m∣+1)​PJ+1∣m∣​(x)+2J+1(J+∣m∣)​PJ−1∣m∣​(x)]​

Using the orthogonality relation for the PJm(x)P_J^m(x)PJm​(x), we find that the above integral will vanish unless J′=J+1J'=J+1J′=J+1 or J′=J−1J'=J-1J′=J−1. This finding leads to the selection rule J′=J±1J'=J\pm1J′=J±1, or ΔJ=±1\Delta J=\pm1ΔJ=±1.

Thus, we have shown that the selection rule for pure rotational spectra in the rigid-rotator approximation is that the molecule must have a permanent dipole moment and that ΔJ=±1\Delta J=\pm1ΔJ=±1 and Δm=0\Delta m=0Δm=0.

（ 转动光谱的选律也和振动光谱类似，来自于递推关系的限制。 ）

6.8 The Precise Values of the Three Components of Angular Momentum Cannot Be Measured Simultaneously

Angular momentum plays a key role not only in the theory of the rigid rotator, but in the theory of the hydrogen atom as well. To keep things general, we’ll use lll for angular momentum and mmm for its z component in this section.

Recall that angular momentum is a vector quantity. We can write the expression of the operator in spherical coordinates:

L^x=−iℏ(−sin⁡ϕ∂∂θ−cotθ cos⁡ϕ∂∂ϕ)L^y=−iℏ(cos⁡ϕ∂∂θ−cotθ sin⁡ϕ∂∂ϕ)L^z=−iℏ∂∂ϕ\hat L_x=-i\hbar \left(-\sin\phi\frac {\partial}{\partial \theta}-cot\theta\ \cos\phi\frac {\partial}{\partial\phi} \right) \\[3mm] \hat L_y=-i\hbar \left(\cos\phi\frac {\partial}{\partial \theta}-cot\theta\ \sin\phi\frac {\partial}{\partial\phi} \right) \\[3mm] \hat L_z=-i\hbar\frac {\partial}{\partial\phi}L^x​=−iℏ(−sinϕ∂θ∂​−cotθ cosϕ∂ϕ∂​)L^y​=−iℏ(cosϕ∂θ∂​−cotθ sinϕ∂ϕ∂​)L^z​=−iℏ∂ϕ∂​

We see that the spherical harmonics are eigenfunctions of L^z\hat L_zL^z​:

L^zYlm(θ,ϕ)=NlmL^zPl∣m∣(cos⁡θ)eimϕ=NlmPl∣m∣(cos⁡θ)L^zeimϕ=ℏmYlm(θ,ϕ)\begin{aligned} \hat L_zY_l^m(\theta,\phi) &=N_{lm}\hat L_zP_l^{|m|}(\cos\theta)e^{im\phi} \\[3mm] &=N_{lm}P_l^{|m|}(\cos\theta)\hat L_ze^{im\phi} \\[3mm] &= \hbar mY_l^m(\theta,\phi) \end{aligned}L^z​Ylm​(θ,ϕ)​=Nlm​L^z​Pl∣m∣​(cosθ)eimϕ=Nlm​Pl∣m∣​(cosθ)L^z​eimϕ=ℏmYlm​(θ,ϕ)​

This equation shows that measured value of LzL_zLz​ are integral multiples of ℏ\hbarℏ.

However, the spherical harmonics are not eigenfunctions of L^x\hat L_xL^x​ or L^y\hat L_yL^y​.

Because the spherical harmonics are simultaneous eigenfunctions of both L^2\hat L^2L^2 and L^z\hat L_zL^z​, we can determine precise values of L2L^2L2 and LzL_zLz​ simultaneously (Section 4.4), which implies that the operators L^2\hat L^2L^2 and L^z\hat L_zL^z​ commute.

We can prove that ∣m∣≤l|m| \le l∣m∣≤l, or that m=0,±1,±2,⋯ ,±lm=0,\pm1,\pm2,\cdots,\pm lm=0,±1,±2,⋯,±l. It follows:

(L^2−L^z2)Ylm(θ,ϕ)=ℏ2[l(l+1)−m2]Ylm(θ,ϕ)(\hat L^2-\hat L_z^2)Y_l^m(\theta,\phi)=\hbar^2[l(l+1)-m^2]Y_l^m(\theta,\phi)(L^2−L^z2​)Ylm​(θ,ϕ)=ℏ2[l(l+1)−m2]Ylm​(θ,ϕ)

Because:

L^2=L^x2+L^y2+L^z2\hat L^2=\hat L_x^2+\hat L_y^2+\hat L_z^2L^2=L^x2​+L^y2​+L^z2​

then:

(L^2−L^z2)Ylm(θ,ϕ)=(L^x2+L^y2)Ylm(θ,ϕ)=ℏ2[l(l+1)−m2]Ylm(θ,ϕ)(\hat L^2-\hat L_z^2)Y_l^m(\theta,\phi)=(\hat L_x^2+\hat L_y^2)Y_l^m(\theta,\phi)=\hbar^2[l(l+1)-m^2]Y_l^m(\theta,\phi)(L^2−L^z2​)Ylm​(θ,ϕ)=(L^x2​+L^y2​)Ylm​(θ,ϕ)=ℏ2[l(l+1)−m2]Ylm​(θ,ϕ)

Thus, the observed values of Lx2+Ly2L_x^2+L_y^2Lx2​+Ly2​ are [l(l+1)−m2]ℏ2[l(l+1)-m^2]\hbar^2[l(l+1)−m2]ℏ2. But because Lx2+Ly2L_x^2+L_y^2Lx2​+Ly2​ is the sum of two squared terms, it cannot be negative, and so we have:

[l(l+1)−m2]ℏ2≥0[l(l+1)-m^2]\hbar^2 \ge 0[l(l+1)−m2]ℏ2≥0

or

l(l+1)≥m2l(l+1) \ge m^2l(l+1)≥m2

Because lll and mmm are integers, so it says that:

∣m∣≤l|m| \le l∣m∣≤l

or that the only possible values of the integer mmm are:

m=0,±1,±2,⋯ ,±lm=0,\pm1,\pm2,\cdots,\pm lm=0,±1,±2,⋯,±l

The equation shows that there are 2l+12l+12l+1 values of mmm for each value of lll.

We can prove:

[L^2,L^x]=[L^2,L^y]=[L^2,L^z]=0[\hat L^2,\hat L_x]=[\hat L^2,\hat L_y]=[\hat L^2,\hat L_z]=0[L^2,L^x​]=[L^2,L^y​]=[L^2,L^z​]=0

But they do not commute among themseles:

[L^x,L^y]=iℏL^z[L^y,L^z]=iℏL^x[L^z,L^x]=iℏL^y\left[\hat L_x,\hat L_y \right] =i\hbar\hat L_z \\[3mm] \left[\hat L_y,\hat L_z \right]=i\hbar\hat L_x \\[3mm] \left[\hat L_z,\hat L_x \right]=i\hbar\hat L_y[L^x​,L^y​]=iℏL^z​[L^y​,L^z​]=iℏL^x​[L^z​,L^x​]=iℏL^y​

It is possible to observe precise values of L2L^2L2 and LzL_zLz​ simultaneously, it is not possible to observe precise values of LxL_xLx​ and LyL_yLy​ simultaneously because they do not commute with each other.

Even though LxL_xLx​ and LyL_yLy​ do not have precise values, they do have an average value:

⟨Lx⟩=⟨Ly⟩=0\langle L_x \rangle=\langle L_y \rangle =0⟨Lx​⟩=⟨Ly​⟩=0

A nice classical interpretation of these results is that LLL precesses about the z axis, mapping out the surface of the cone shown there. The average values of ⟨Lx⟩\langle L_x \rangle⟨Lx​⟩ and ⟨Ly⟩\langle L_y \rangle⟨Ly​⟩ are zero. This picture is in nice accord with the uncertainty principle: by specifying LzL_zLz​ exactly, we have a complete uncertainty in the angle ϕ\phiϕ associated with LzL_zLz​.

Before leaving this section, we should address the following question: What is so special about the z direction? The answer is that nothing at all is special about the z direction. We could have chosen either the x or y direction as the unique direction and all the above results would be the same, except for exchanging x or y for z.

（ 角动量平方算符和角动量z轴分量算符对易，因此可以同时测得角动量大小和它在z轴分量的大小。但是在x-y平面的方向则无法确定，因为L^z\hat L_zL^z​与L^x/L^y\hat L_x/\hat L_yL^x​/L^y​均不对易，所以它的图像很直观地对应于Figure 6.6中的圆锥图形。 ）

总结

本章讨论了刚性转子模型和转动光谱，总体思路实际上和上一章的振动光谱有很多相似。

本章章末附录中讨论了用算符方法计算角动量平方算符L^2\hat L^2L^2和角动量z轴分量算符L^z\hat L_zL^z​的本征值关系的做法，同样是使用阶梯算符对球谐函数做处理，很自然就导出了mmm和lll的关系，值得一看。

entry.title: 《Quantum Chemistry》章末总结5
entry.content:
第五章讲谐振子，这是量子力学的核心模型之一，同时学习振动光谱。

Chapter 5 The Harmonic Oscillator and Vibrational Spectroscopy

5.1 A Harmonic Oscillator Obeys Hooke’s Law

Consider a mass mmm connected to a wall by a spring, as shown in Figure 5.1.

Suppose further that no gravitational force is acting on mmm so that the only force is due to the spring.

If we let l0l_0l0​ be the equilibrium, or undistorted, length of the spring, then the restoring force must be some function of the displacement of the spring from its equilibrium length. Let this displacement be denoted by x=l−l0x=l-l_0x=l−l0​, where lll is the length of the spring. The simplest assumption we can make about the force on m as a function of the displacement is that the force is directly proportional to the displacement and to write:

f=−k(l−l0)=−kxf=-k(l-l_0)=-kxf=−k(l−l0​)=−kx

The negative sign indicates that the force points to the right in Figure 5.1 if the spring is compressed (l<l0l<l_0l<l0​) and points to the left ifthe spring is stretched (l>l0l>l_0l>l0​). The equation is called Hooke’s law and the (positive) proportionality constant kkk is called the force constant of the spring.

Newton’s equation with a Hooke’s law force is:

md2ldt2=−k(l−l0)m\frac {d^2l}{dt^2}=-k(l-l_0)mdt2d2l​=−k(l−l0​)

If we let x=l−l0x=l-l_0x=l−l0​, then we have:

md2xdt2+kx=0m\frac {d^2x}{dt^2}+kx=0mdt2d2x​+kx=0

The general solution to this equation is:

x(t)=c1sinωt+c2cosωtx(t)=c_1sin\omega t+c_2cos\omega tx(t)=c1​sinωt+c2​cosωt

where:

ω=(km)1/2\omega = \left(\frac km \right)^{1/2}ω=(mk​)1/2

Suppose we stretch the spring so that its displacement is A and then let go. The initial velocity is zero and we have:

x(0)=c2=Ax(0)=c_2=Ax(0)=c2​=A

(dxdt)t=0=0=c1ω\left(\frac {dx}{dt} \right)_{t=0}=0=c_1\omega(dtdx​)t=0​=0=c1​ω

And so:

x(t)=Acosωtx(t)=Acos\omega tx(t)=Acosωt

The displacement versus time is plotted in Figure 5.2, which shows that the mass oscillates back and forth between AAA and −A-A−A with a frequency ω\omegaω radians per second, or ν=ω/2π\nu=\omega/2\piν=ω/2π cycles per second. The quantity AAA is called the amplitude of the vibration.

5.2 The Energy of a Harmonic Oscillator Is Conserved

Let’s look at the total energy of a harmonic oscillator. The potential energy is:

V(x)=−∫f(x)dx+constantV(x)=-\int f(x)dx+constantV(x)=−∫f(x)dx+constant

We can see that:

V(x)=k2x2+constantV(x)=\frac {k}{2}x^2+constantV(x)=2k​x2+constant

The constant term here is an arbitrary constant that can be used to fix the zero of energy. If we choose the potential energy of the system to be zero when the spring is undistorted (x=0)(x=0)(x=0), then we have:

V(x)=k2x2=12kA2cos2ωt\begin{aligned} V(x) &=\frac k2x^2 \\[3mm] &=\frac 12kA^2cos^2\omega t \end{aligned}V(x)​=2k​x2=21​kA2cos2ωt​

for the potential energy associated with a simple harmonic oscillator.

The kinetic energy is:

T=12m(dldt)2=12m(dxdt)2=12mω2A2sin2ωt\begin{aligned} T &=\frac 12m \left(\frac {dl}{dt} \right)^2=\frac 12m \left(\frac {dx}{dt} \right)^2 \\[3mm] &=\frac 12m\omega^2A^2sin^2\omega t \end{aligned}T​=21​m(dtdl​)2=21​m(dtdx​)2=21​mω2A2sin2ωt​

Both TTT and VVV are plotted in Figure 5.3. The total energy is:

E=T+V=12kA2cos2ωt+12mω2A2sin2ωt=12kA2\begin{aligned} E=T+V &=\frac 12kA^2cos^2\omega t+\frac 12m\omega^2A^2sin^2\omega t \\[3mm] &=\frac 12kA^2 \end{aligned}E=T+V​=21​kA2cos2ωt+21​mω2A2sin2ωt=21​kA2​

Thus, we see that the total energy is a constant and, in particular, is equal to the potential energy at its largest displacement, where the kinetic energy is zero.

Each oscillates between +A+A+A and −A-A−A but in such a way that their sum is always a constant. We say that the total energy is conserved and that the system is a conservative system.

and introduce x=x2−x1−l0x=x_2-x_1-l_0x=x2​−x1​−l0​, then we have:

5.6 The Harmonic Oscillator Accounts for the Infrared Spectrum of a Diatomic Molecule

The vibrational energy levels of the diatomic molecule are given by:

A diatomic molecule can make a transition from one vibrational energy state to another by absorbing or emitting electromagnetic radiation whose observed frequency satisfies the Bohr frequency condition:

We will prove in Chapter 8 that the harmonic-oscillator model allows transitions only between adjacent energy states, so that we have the condition that Δv=±1\Delta v=\pm1Δv=±1. Such a condition is called a selection rule.

Thus, the observed frequency of the radiation absorbed is:

So this model predicts that the spectrum consists of just one line. This
prediction is in good accord with experiment, and this line is called the fundamental vibrational frequency. For diatomic molecules, these lines occur at around 101410^{14}1014 Hz, which is in the infrared region.

5.11 The Vibrations of Polyatomic Molecules Are Represented by Normal Coordinates

The vibrational spectra of polyatomic molecules turn out to be easily understood in the harmonic-oscillator approximation. The key point is the introduction of normal coordinates, which we discuss in this section.

Consider a molecule containing N nuclei. A complete specification of this molecule in space requires 3N coordinates, three cartesian coordinates for each nucleus. We say that the N-atomic molecule has a total of 3N degrees of freedom.

Of these 3N coordinates, three can be used to specify the center of mass of the molecule. Motion along these three coordinates corresponds to translational motion of the center of mass of the molecule, and so we call these three coordinates translational degrees of freedom.

（ 平动自由度是由质心的运动决定的。 ）

It requires two coordinates to specify the orientation of a linear molecule about its center of mass and three coordinates to specify the orientation of a nonlinear molecule about its center of mass. Because motion along these coordinates corresponds to rotational motion, we say that a linear molecule has two degrees of rotational freedom and that a nonlinear molecule has three degrees of rotational freedom.

（ 空间中的转动可以用欧拉角来描述，用Pitch-Yaw-Roll三个角度就可以描述任何转动。对于线性双原子分子来说，由于分子键轴是C∞C_{\infin}C∞​轴，所以不需要Roll角，只需要其他两个角度就可以描述其转动，因此是两个转动自由度。 ）

The remaining coordinates (3N-5 for a linear molecule and 3N-6 for a nonlinear molecule) specify the relative positions of the N nuclei. Because motion along these coordinates corresponds to vibrational motion, we say that a linear molecule has 3N-5 vibrational degrees of freedom and that a nonlinear molecule has 3N-6 vibrational degrees of freedom.

（ 总自由度减去平动和转动，剩下的就是振动自由度了。 ）

In the absence of external fields, the energy of a molecule does not depend upon the position of its center of mass or its orientation. The potential energy of a polyatomic molecule is therefore a function of only the 3N-5 or 3N-6 vibrational coordinates.

If we let the displacements about the equilibrium values of these coordinates be denoted by x1,x2,⋯ ,xNvibx_1,x_2,\cdots,x_{N_{vib}}x1​,x2​,⋯,xNvib​​ where NvibN_{vib}Nvib​ is the number of vibrational degrees of freedom, then the potential energy is given by:

ΔV=V(x1,x2,⋯ ,xNvib)−V(0,0,⋯ ,0)=12∑i=1Nvib∑j=1Nvib(∂2V∂xi∂xj)xixj+⋯=12∑i=1Nvib∑j=1Nvibfijxixj+⋯\begin{aligned} \Delta V &=V(x_1,x_2,\cdots,x_{N_{vib}})-V(0,0,\cdots,0) \\[3mm] &=\frac 12\sum_{i=1}^{N_{vib}}\sum_{j=1}^{N_{vib}} \left(\frac {\partial^2V}{\partial x_i\partial x_j} \right)x_ix_j+\cdots \\[3mm] &=\frac 12\sum_{i=1}^{N_{vib}}\sum_{j=1}^{N_{vib}}f_{ij}x_ix_j+\cdots \end{aligned}ΔV​=V(x1​,x2​,⋯,xNvib​​)−V(0,0,⋯,0)=21​i=1∑Nvib​​j=1∑Nvib​​(∂xi​∂xj​∂2V​)xi​xj​+⋯=21​i=1∑Nvib​​j=1∑Nvib​​fij​xi​xj​+⋯​

In general, there are other terms that contain higher powers of xix_ixi​, but these anharmonic terms are neglected here.

The presence of the cross terms in the equation makes the solution of the corresponding Schrödinger equation very difficult to obtain. A theorem of classical mechanics, however, allows us to eliminate all the cross terms. A straightforward procedure using matrix algebra can be used to find a new set of coordinates {QjQ_jQj​}, such that:

ΔV=12∑j=1NvibFjQj2\Delta V=\frac 12\sum_{j=1}^{N_{vib}}F_jQ_j^2ΔV=21​j=1∑Nvib​​Fj​Qj2​

These new coordinates are called normal coordinates or normal modes. In terms of normal coordinates, the vibrational Hamiltonian operator is:

H^vib=−∑j=1Nvibℏ22μjd2dQj2+12∑j=1NvibFjQj2\hat H_{vib}=-\sum_{j=1}^{N_{vib}}\frac {\hbar^2}{2\mu_j}\frac {d^2}{dQ_j^2}+\frac 12\sum_{j=1}^{N_{vib}}F_jQ_j^2H^vib​=−j=1∑Nvib​​2μj​ℏ2​dQj2​d2​+21​j=1∑Nvib​​Fj​Qj2​

Recall from Section 3.9 that if a Hamiltonian operator can be written as a sum of independent terms, the total wave function is a product of individual wave functions and the energy is a sum of independent energies:

H^vib=∑j=1NvibH^vib,j=∑j=1Nvib(−ℏ22μjd2dQj2+12FjQj2)ψvib(Q1,Q2,⋯ ,Qvib)=ψvib,1(Q1)ψvib,2(Q2)⋯ψvib,Nvib(QNvib)\hat H_{vib}=\sum_{j=1}^{N_{vib}}\hat H_{vib,j}=\sum_{j=1}^{N_{vib}} \left(-\frac {\hbar^2}{2\mu_j}\frac {d^2}{dQ_j^2}+\frac 12F_jQ_j^2 \right) \\[3mm] \psi_{vib}(Q_1,Q_2,\cdots,Q_{vib})=\psi_{vib,1}(Q_1)\psi_{vib,2}(Q_2)\cdots\psi_{vib,N_{vib}}(Q_{N_{vib}})H^vib​=j=1∑Nvib​​H^vib,j​=j=1∑Nvib​​(−2μj​ℏ2​dQj2​d2​+21​Fj​Qj2​)ψvib​(Q1​,Q2​,⋯,Qvib​)=ψvib,1​(Q1​)ψvib,2​(Q2​)⋯ψvib,Nvib​​(QNvib​​)

and:

Evib=∑j=1Nvibhνj(νj+12)each νj=0,1,2,⋯E_{vib}=\sum_{j=1}^{N_{vib}}h\nu_j \left(\nu_j+\frac 12 \right) \quad each\ \nu_j=0,1,2,\cdotsEvib​=j=1∑Nvib​​hνj​(νj​+21​)each νj​=0,1,2,⋯

（ 哈密顿量可以写成几个独立组分的哈密顿量的加和，而总波函数可以写成几个独立组分波函数的乘积。结果是，总能量为各独立部分的能量之和，见3.9节。

一般形式下的哈密顿量的势能项是耦合的，这使得求解薛定谔方程变得非常困难。引入简正坐标的目的就是为了消去交叉项，即“解耦”。分离变量后，方程就变成了多个谐振子方程，分子总的振动可以看作多个简正模的叠加。 ）

5.12 The Harmonic-Oscillator Selection Rule Is Δv=±1\Delta v=\pm1Δv=±1

In this section, we shall discuss a selection rule. We shall show in Section 8.6 that if a harmonic oscillator is irradiated with electromagnetic radiation propagating in the z direction, then the probability that the oscillator makes a transition from state vvv to state v′v'v′ is proportional to the square of the integral:

⟨v∣μz∣v′⟩=∫−∞∞dxψv(x)μz(x)ψv′(x)\langle v|\mu_z|v' \rangle =\int_{-\infin}^{\infin}dx \psi_v(x)\mu_z(x)\psi_{v'}(x)⟨v∣μz​∣v′⟩=∫−∞∞​dxψv​(x)μz​(x)ψv′​(x)

where μz\mu_zμz​ is the z component of the dipole moment. This type of integral, which occurs frequently in spectroscopy, is called a dipole transition moment.

We now expand μz(x)\mu_z(x)μz​(x) about the equilibrium nuclear separation:

μz(x)=μ0+(dμdx)0x+⋯\mu_z(x)=\mu_0+ \left(\frac {d\mu}{dx}\right)_0x+\cdotsμz​(x)=μ0​+(dxdμ​)0​x+⋯

where μ0\mu_0μ0​ is the dipole moment at the equilibrium bond length and xxx is the displacement from that equilibrium value. Thus, when x=0,μz=μ0x=0,\mu_z=\mu_0x=0,μz​=μ0​. We substitute the equation into the expression of dipole transition moment:

⟨v∣μz∣v′⟩=μ0⟨v∣v′⟩+(dμdx)0⟨v∣x∣v′⟩\langle v|\mu_z|v' \rangle = \mu_0\langle v|v' \rangle + \left(\frac {d\mu}{dx}\right)_0 \langle v|x|v' \rangle⟨v∣μz​∣v′⟩=μ0​⟨v∣v′⟩+(dxdμ​)0​⟨v∣x∣v′⟩

The first integral here vanishes if v≠v′v\ne v'v​=v′ due to the orthogonality of the harmonic-oscillator wave functions. The second integral can be evaluated in general by using:

ξHv(ξ)=vHv−1(ξ)+12Hv+1(ξ)(ξ=α1/2x)\xi H_v(\xi)=vH_{v-1}(\xi)+\frac 12H_{v+1}(\xi) \quad (\xi=\alpha^{1/2}x)ξHv​(ξ)=vHv−1​(ξ)+21​Hv+1​(ξ)(ξ=α1/2x)

so we obtain:

⟨v∣μz∣v′⟩=NvNv′α(dμdξ)0∫−∞∞Hv′(ξ)[vHv−1(ξ)+12Hv+1(ξ)]e−ξ2dξ\langle v|\mu_z|v' \rangle = \frac {N_vN_{v'}}{\alpha} \left(\frac {d\mu}{d\xi}\right)_0 \int_{-\infin}^{\infin}H_{v'}(\xi) \left[vH_{v-1}(\xi)+\frac 12H_{v+1}(\xi) \right]e^{-\xi^2}d\xi⟨v∣μz​∣v′⟩=αNv​Nv′​​(dξdμ​)0​∫−∞∞​Hv′​(ξ)[vHv−1​(ξ)+21​Hv+1​(ξ)]e−ξ2dξ

Using now the orthogonality property of the Hermite polynomials, we see that ⟨v∣μz∣v′⟩\langle v|\mu_z|v' \rangle⟨v∣μz​∣v′⟩ vanishes unless v′=v±1v'=v\pm1v′=v±1. Thus, the selection rule for vibrational transitions under the harmonic-oscillator approximation is that Δv=±1\Delta v=\pm1Δv=±1.

（ 我们可以发现选律的产生实际上是因为厄米多项式的递推公式的限制。 ）

In addition, the factor (dμ/dξ)0(d\mu/d\xi)_0(dμ/dξ)0​ in front of the transition moment integral reminds us that the dipole moment of the molecule must vary during a vibration, or the transition will not take place.

A selection rule for vibrational absorption spectroscopy is that the dipole moment of the molecule must vary during the normal mode motion. When this is so, the normal mode is said to be infrared active. Otherwise, it is infrared inactive.

The normal modes of H2OH_2OH2​O are as follows:

Note that the dipole moment changes during the motion of all three normal modes, so all three normal modes of H2OH_2OH2​O are infrared active. Therefore, H2OH_2OH2​O has three bands in its infrared spectrum.

（ 简正模的偶极矩发生变化才会产生跃迁偶极矩，即具有红外活性，才会在红外光谱上显示谱线。 ）

总结

本章最后的附录中介绍了代数法解决谐振子的薛定谔方程，构造升/降阶算符来求解波函数。在此处略去。

从这章开始，随着量子力学基本模型和光谱的引入，内容难度也比之前高了不少，具体的数理计算过程可以暂时放下，不过如果能结合计算过程来思考，很多东西的来龙去脉就会更清晰可见。

entry.title: 《Quantum Chemistry》章末总结4
entry.content:
第四章介绍量子力学公设。

Chapter 4 The Postulates and General Principles of Quantum Mechanics

4.1 The State of a System Is Completely Specified by lts Wave Function

Classical mechanics deals with quantities called dynamical variables, such as position, momentum, angular momentum, and energy. A measurable dynamical variable is called an observable.

The classical-mechanical state of a one-body system at any particular time is specified completely by the three position coordinates (x,y,z)(x,y,z)(x,y,z) and the three momenta or velocities (vx,vy,vz)(v_x,v_y,v_z)(vx​,vy​,vz​) at that time.

Classical mechanics provides a method for calculating the trajectory of a particle in terms of the forces acting upon the particle through Newton’s equations.

If there are NNN particles in the system, then it takes 3N3N3N coordinates and 3N3N3N velocities to specify the state of the system. We should suspect immediately that this is not going to be so in quantum mechanics because the uncertainty principle tells us that we cannot specify or determine the position and momentum of a particle simultaneously with infinite precision. This leads us to our first postulate of quantum mechanics.

  • Postulate 1: The state of a quantum-mechanical system is completely specified by a function Ψ(r,t)\Psi(\boldsymbol r,t)Ψ(r,t) that depends on the coordinates of the particle and on time. This function, called the wave function or state function, has the important property that Ψ∗(r,t)Ψ(r,t)dxdydz\Psi^*(\boldsymbol r,t)\Psi(\boldsymbol r,t)dxdydzΨ∗(r,t)Ψ(r,t)dxdydz is the probability that the particle lies in the volume element dxdydzdxdydzdxdydz located at r\boldsymbol rr at time ttt.

Postulate 1 says that the state of a quantum-mechanical system such as two electrons is completely specified by this function and that nothing else is required.

Because the square of the wave function has a probabilistic interpretation, it must satisfy certain physical requirements.

In addition to being normalized, or at least normalizable, because Ψ∗(r,t)Ψ(r,t)dτ\Psi^*(\boldsymbol r,t)\Psi(\boldsymbol r,t)d\tauΨ∗(r,t)Ψ(r,t)dτ is a probability, we require that Ψ(r,t)\Psi(\boldsymbol r,t)Ψ(r,t) and its first spatial derivative be single-valued, continuous, and finite. We summarize these requirements by saying that Ψ(r,t)\Psi(\boldsymbol r,t)Ψ(r,t) must be well behaved.

（ 公设一说明了波函数蕴含了系统的一切性质，波函数的平方表示粒子的概率密度。 ）

4.2 Quantum-Mechanical Operators Represent Classical-Mechanical Variables

  • Postulate 2: To every observable in classical mechanics there corresponds a linear operator in quantum mechanics.

（ 公设二是易于理解的，算符作用于波函数将力学量的求解问题转化为本征值问题，每个可观测量都有对应的线性算符。书中说量子力学中都是线性算符，其实不准确，量子力学中也用到一些非线性算符，只不过它们不对应可观测的物理量。

另外，这一条公设将会在4.5小节更严谨地加以修正。 ）

4.3 Observable Quantities Must Be Eigenvalues of Quantum-Mechanical Operators

  • Postulate 3: In any measurement of the observable associated with the operator A^\hat AA^, the only values that will ever be observed are the eigenvalues aaa, which satisfy the eigenvalue equation:

A^Ψa=aΨa\hat A\Psi_a=a\Psi_aA^Ψa​=aΨa​

Generally, an operator will have a set of eigenfunctions and eigenvalues, and we indicate this by writing:

A^Ψn=anΨn\hat A \Psi_n=a_n\Psi_nA^Ψn​=an​Ψn​

Thus, in any experiment designed to measure the observable corresponding to A^\hat AA^, the only values we find are a1,a2,a3,⋯a_1,a_2,a_3,\cdotsa1​,a2​,a3​,⋯, The set of eigenvalues {ana_nan​} of an operator A^\hat AA^ is called the spectrum of A^\hat AA^.

Because of the equation ΔE=hν\Delta E=h\nuΔE=hν, we see that the experimentally observed spectrum of the system is intimately related to the mathematical spectrum. This is the motivation for calling the set of eigenvalues of an operator its spectrum, and this is also why the Schrödinger equation is a special eigenvalue equation.

The particle in a box is a bound system, and for bound systems the spectrum is discrete. For an unbound system, the spectrum is continuous.

For other systems, such as a particle in a box with finite walls (Figure 4.1), the spectrum can have both discrete and continuous parts.

（ 公设三与公设二相联系，把力学量求解问题转化为本征值问题。 ）

It is important to realize that the {Ψn\Psi_nΨn​} are very special functions, and it is possible that a system will not be in one of these states. In fact, if we were to measure the energy of each member of a collection of similarly described systems, all in the state described by Ψ\PsiΨ, then we would observe a distribution of energies, but each member of this distribution will be one of the energies EnE_nEn​ This leads to our fourth postulate.

  • Postulate 4: If a system is in a state described by a normalized wave function Ψ\PsiΨ, then the average value of the observable corresponding to A^\hat AA^ is given by:

⟨a⟩=∫−∞∞Ψ∗A^Ψdτ\left\langle a \right\rangle=\int_{-\infin}^{\infin}\Psi^*\hat A\Psi d\tau⟨a⟩=∫−∞∞​Ψ∗A^Ψdτ

Thus, Postulate 3 says that the only value that we measure is the value ana_nan​. Often, however, the system is not in a state described by an eigenfunction, and one measures a distribution of values whose average is given by Postulate 4.

（ 如果系统的状态可以用本征函数描述，那么我们通过实验测得的值就是算符对应的力学量；不过有时候系统的状态函数是一个非本征函数，此时公设四指出：实验测得的可观测量为力学量的平均值/期待值。 ）

4.4 The Commutator of Two Operators Plays a Central Role in the Uncertainty Principle

When two operators act sequentially on a function, as in A^B^f(x)\hat A\hat Bf(x)A^B^f(x), we apply each operator in turn, working from right to left:

A^B^f(x)=A^[B^f(x)]=A^h(x)\hat A\hat Bf(x)=\hat A[\hat Bf(x)]=\hat Ah(x)A^B^f(x)=A^[B^f(x)]=A^h(x)

where h(x)=B^f(x)h(x)=\hat Bf(x)h(x)=B^f(x). An important difference between operators and ordinary algebraic quantities is that operators do not necessarily commute:

A^B^f(x)=B^A^f(x)(commutative)A^B^f(x)≠B^A^f(x)(noncommutative)\hat A\hat Bf(x)=\hat B\hat Af(x) \quad (commutative) \\ \hat A\hat Bf(x) \neq \hat B\hat Af(x) \quad (noncommutative)A^B^f(x)=B^A^f(x)(commutative)A^B^f(x)​=B^A^f(x)(noncommutative)

We called the commutator, [A^,B^][\hat A,\hat B][A^,B^], of A^\hat AA^ and B^\hat BB^:

[A^,B^]=A^B^−B^A^[\hat A,\hat B]=\hat A\hat B-\hat B\hat A[A^,B^]=A^B^−B^A^

If [A^,B^]f(x)=0[\hat A,\hat B]f(x)=0[A^,B^]f(x)=0 for all f(x)f(x)f(x) on which the commutator acts, then we write that [A^,B^]=0[\hat A,\hat B]=0[A^,B^]=0 and we say that A^\hat AA^ and B^\hat BB^ commute.

If two operators do not commute, then their corresponding observable quantities do not have simultaneously well-defined values, and in fact:

σA2σB2≥−14(∫ψ∗[A^,B^]ψdx)2\sigma_A^2\sigma_B^2 \ge -\frac 14 \left(\int \psi^* [\hat A,\hat B] \psi dx \right)^2σA2​σB2​≥−41​(∫ψ∗[A^,B^]ψdx)2

where σA2\sigma_A^2σA2​ and σB2\sigma_B^2σB2​ are:

σA2=∫ψ∗(A^−⟨a⟩)2ψdxσB2=∫ψ∗(B^−⟨b⟩)2ψdx\sigma_A^2 = \int \psi^*(\hat A-\left\langle a \right\rangle)^2 \psi dx \\ \sigma_B^2 = \int \psi^*(\hat B-\left\langle b \right\rangle)^2 \psi dxσA2​=∫ψ∗(A^−⟨a⟩)2ψdxσB2​=∫ψ∗(B^−⟨b⟩)2ψdx

If A^\hat AA^ and B^\hat BB^ are the momentum and position operators. In the case:

[A^,B^]=[P^x,X^]=−iℏI^[\hat A,\hat B]=[\hat P_x,\hat X]=-i\hbar\hat I[A^,B^]=[P^x​,X^]=−iℏI^

where I^\hat II^ is the identity operator.

And:

σp2σx2≥−14(−iℏ)2=ℏ24\sigma_p^2\sigma_x^2 \ge -\frac 14(-i\hbar)^2=\frac {\hbar^2}{4}σp2​σx2​≥−41​(−iℏ)2=4ℏ2​

By taking the square root of both sides, we have:

σpσx≥ℏ2\sigma_p\sigma_x \ge \frac {\hbar}{2}σp​σx​≥2ℏ​

which is the Heisenberg uncertainty principle for momentum and position.

4.5 Quantum-Mechanical Operators Must Be Hermitian Operators

We have seen that wave functions, and operators generally, are complex
quantities, but certainly the eigenvalues must be real quantities if they are to correspond to the result of experimental measurement:

A^∗ψ∗=a∗ψ∗=aψ∗\hat A^*\psi^*=a^*\psi^*=a\psi^*A^∗ψ∗=a∗ψ∗=aψ∗

where the equality a∗=aa^*=aa∗=a recognizes that aaa is real. So:

∫ψA^∗ψ∗dx=a∫ψψ∗dx=a=∫ψ∗A^ψdx\int \psi\hat A^*\psi^*dx = a\int\psi\psi^*dx = a =\int \psi^* \hat A\psi dx∫ψA^∗ψ∗dx=a∫ψψ∗dx=a=∫ψ∗A^ψdx

The operator A^\hat AA^ must satisfy the equation to assure that its eigenvalues are real. An operator that satisfies the equation for any well-behaved function is called a Hermitian operator. Thus, we can write the definition of a Hermitian operator as an operator that satisfies the relation:

∫−∞∞f∗A^fdx=∫−∞∞fA^∗f∗dx\int_{-\infin}^{\infin} f^*\hat Afdx = \int_{-\infin}^{\infin} f {\hat A}^* f^* dx∫−∞∞​f∗A^fdx=∫−∞∞​fA^∗f∗dx

Hermitian operators have real eigenvalues. Postulate 2 should be modified to read as follows:

  • Postulate 2’: To every observable in classical mechanics there corresponds a linem; Hermitian operator in quantum mechanics.

A more general definition of a Hermitian operator is given by:

∫−∞∞dxfm∗(x)A^fn(x)=∫−∞∞dxfn(x)A^∗fm∗(x)\int_{-\infin}^{\infin} dx f_m^*(x) \hat A f_n(x) = \int_{-\infin}^{\infin}dx f_n(x) {\hat A}^* f^*_m(x)∫−∞∞​dxfm∗​(x)A^fn​(x)=∫−∞∞​dxfn​(x)A^∗fm∗​(x)

where fn(x)f_n(x)fn​(x) and fm(x)f_m(x)fm​(x) are any two well-behaved functions. We shall use this definition quite often.

（ 厄米算符对应的本征值为实数，所以很容易理解为什么其在量子力学中十分重要了，因为本征值为实数才有物理意义。 ）

This is a good time to introduce a notation that is extremely widely used. Let {fn(x)f_n(x)fn​(x)} be some set of well-behaved functions that we label by an integer nnn. These functions might, but not necessarily, be the eigenfunctions of some operator O^\hat OO^.

In this new notational scheme, we shall express fn(x)f_n(x)fn​(x) as ∣n⟩|n\rangle∣n⟩. Instead of denoting the complex conjugate of fn(x)f_n(x)fn​(x) by ∣n⟩∗|n\rangle^*∣n⟩∗, we denote it by ⟨n∣\langle n|⟨n∣. The integral of fn∗(x)fn(x)f_n^*(x)f_n(x)fn∗​(x)fn​(x) in this notation is expressed as ⟨n∣n⟩\langle n|n \rangle⟨n∣n⟩ , or:

∫−∞∞dxfn∗(x)fn(x)=⟨n∣n⟩\int_{-\infin}^{\infin} dx f_n^*(x)f_n(x)= \langle n|n \rangle∫−∞∞​dxfn∗​(x)fn​(x)=⟨n∣n⟩

Normalization corresponds to writing ⟨n∣n⟩=1\langle n|n \rangle=1⟨n∣n⟩=1. More generally:

∫−∞∞dxfm∗(x)fn(x)=⟨m∣n⟩\int_{-\infin}^{\infin} dx f_m^*(x)f_n(x)= \langle m|n \rangle∫−∞∞​dxfm∗​(x)fn​(x)=⟨m∣n⟩

Continuing, for an operator A^\hat AA^ we write:

∫−∞∞dxfm∗(x)A^fn(x)=⟨m∣A^∣n⟩\int_{-\infin}^{\infin} dx f_m^*(x) \hat A f_n(x)= \langle m|\hat A |n \rangle∫−∞∞​dxfm∗​(x)A^fn​(x)=⟨m∣A^∣n⟩

and so A^\hat AA^ is a Hermitian operator if:

⟨m∣A^∣n⟩=⟨n∣A^∣m⟩∗\langle m|\hat A |n \rangle = \langle n|\hat A |m \rangle^*⟨m∣A^∣n⟩=⟨n∣A^∣m⟩∗

This notation is due to the British physicist Paul Dirac. The quantities ∣n⟩|n\rangle∣n⟩ are called kets, and the ⟨m∣\langle m|⟨m∣ are called bras. This nomenclature arises from the fact that integrals are denoted by bra‾ c kets‾\underline{bra} \ c\ \underline{kets}bra​ c kets​, ⟨m∣A^∣n⟩\langle m|\hat A|n \rangle⟨m∣A^∣n⟩. The notational scheme is called Dirac notation or bracket notation.

4.6 The Eigenfunctions of Hermitian Operators Are Orthogonal

We have been led naturally to the definition and use of Hemiitian operators by requiring that quantum-mechanical operators have real eigenvalues. Not only are the eigenvalues of Hermitian operators real, but their eigenfunctions satisfy a rather special condition as well. Consider the two eigenvalue equations:

A^ψn=anψnA^ψm=amψm\hat A\psi_n = a_n\psi_n \quad \hat A\psi_m = a_m\psi_mA^ψn​=an​ψn​A^ψm​=am​ψm​

We multiply the first of equations by ψm∗\psi_m^*ψm∗​ and integrate; then we take the complex conjugate of the second, multiply by ψn\psi_nψn​ and integrate to obtain:

⟨m∣A^∣n⟩=an⟨m∣n⟩⟨n∣A^∣m⟩∗=am∗⟨m∣n⟩\langle m|\hat A|n \rangle = a_n\langle m|n \rangle \\ \langle n|\hat A|m \rangle^* = a_m^*\langle m|n \rangle⟨m∣A^∣n⟩=an​⟨m∣n⟩⟨n∣A^∣m⟩∗=am∗​⟨m∣n⟩

and:

⟨m∣A^∣n⟩−⟨n∣A^∣m⟩∗=(an−am∗)⟨m∣n⟩\langle m|\hat A|n \rangle - \langle n|\hat A|m \rangle^*=(a_n-a_m^*)\langle m|n \rangle⟨m∣A^∣n⟩−⟨n∣A^∣m⟩∗=(an​−am∗​)⟨m∣n⟩

Because A^\hat AA^ is Hermitian, so we have:

(an−am∗)⟨m∣n⟩=0(a_n-a_m^*)\langle m|n \rangle =0(an​−am∗​)⟨m∣n⟩=0

When n=mn=mn=m, the integral is unity by normalization and so we have:

an=an∗a_n=a_n^*an​=an∗​

which is just another proof that the eigenvalues are real.

When n≠mn \neq mn​=m and if the system is nondegenerate, we have:

⟨m∣n⟩=0\langle m|n \rangle =0⟨m∣n⟩=0

A set of eigenfunctions that satisfies the condition in the equation is said to be orthogonal. We have just proved that the eigenfunctions of a Hermitian operator are orthogonal, at least for a nondegenerate system.

A set of functions that are both normalized and orthogonal to each other is called an orthonormal set. We can express the condition of orthonormality by writing:

⟨m∣n⟩=δnm\langle m|n \rangle = \delta_{nm}⟨m∣n⟩=δnm​

where:

δnm={1m=n0m≠n\delta_{nm}=\left\{\begin{aligned} 1 \quad m=n \\ 0 \quad m\neq n \end{aligned} \right .δnm​={1m=n0m​=n​

The symbol δnm\delta_{nm}δnm​ occurs frequently and is called the Kronecker delta.

Let’s consider the case in which two states, described by ψ1\psi_1ψ1​ and ψ2\psi_2ψ2​, have the same eigenvalue a1a_1a1​:

A^∣ψ1⟩=a1∣ψ1⟩A^∣ψ2⟩=a1∣ψ2⟩\hat A|\psi_1\rangle=a_1|\psi_1\rangle \quad \hat A|\psi_2\rangle=a_1|\psi_2\rangleA^∣ψ1​⟩=a1​∣ψ1​⟩A^∣ψ2​⟩=a1​∣ψ2​⟩

Now let’s consider a linear combination of ψ1\psi_1ψ1​ and ψ2\psi_2ψ2​, say ϕ=c1ψ1+c2ψ2\phi =c_1\psi_1+c_2\psi_2ϕ=c1​ψ1​+c2​ψ2​. Then:

A^∣ϕ⟩=c1A^∣ψ1⟩+c2A^∣ψ2⟩=a1(c1∣ψ1⟩+c2∣ψ2⟩)=a1∣ϕ⟩\hat A|\phi\rangle =c_1 \hat A|\psi_1\rangle+c_2\hat A|\psi_2\rangle = a_1(c_1|\psi_1\rangle +c_2|\psi_2\rangle)=a_1|\phi\rangleA^∣ϕ⟩=c1​A^∣ψ1​⟩+c2​A^∣ψ2​⟩=a1​(c1​∣ψ1​⟩+c2​∣ψ2​⟩)=a1​∣ϕ⟩

Thus, we see that if ψ1\psi_1ψ1​ and ψ2\psi_2ψ2​ describe a two-fold degenerate state with eigenvalue a1a_1a1​, then any linear combination of ψ1\psi_1ψ1​ and ψ2\psi_2ψ2​ is also an eigenfunction with eigenvalue a1a_1a1​.

It is convenient to choose two linear combinations of ψ1\psi_1ψ1​ and ψ2\psi_2ψ2​, call them ϕ1\phi_1ϕ1​ and ϕ2\phi_2ϕ2​, such that:

⟨ϕ1∣ϕ2⟩=0\langle \phi_1|\phi_2 \rangle =0⟨ϕ1​∣ϕ2​⟩=0

（ 对于一个简并系统，ψ1\psi_1ψ1​和ψ2\psi_2ψ2​的线性组合仍然具有相同的本征值，所以我们可以通过一些手段让线性组合后的结果满足正交归一，这种方法就是线性代数里讲的Gram-Schmidt正交化。 ）

So even if there is a degeneracy, we can construct the eigenfunctions of a Hermitian operator such that they are orthonormal and say that they form an orthonormal set.

4.7 If Two Operators Commute, They Have a Mutual Set of Eigenfunctions

Suppose that two operators A^\hat AA^ and B^\hat BB^ have the same set of eigenfunctions, so that we have:

A^∣ϕn⟩=an∣ϕn⟩B^∣ϕn⟩=bn∣ϕn⟩\hat A|\phi_n\rangle = a_n|\phi_n\rangle \quad \hat B|\phi_n\rangle = b_n|\phi_n\rangleA^∣ϕn​⟩=an​∣ϕn​⟩B^∣ϕn​⟩=bn​∣ϕn​⟩

We shall prove that if two operators have the same set of eigenfunctions, then they necessarily commute. To prove this, we must show that:

[A^,B^]f(x)=0[\hat A,\hat B]f(x)=0[A^,B^]f(x)=0

for an arbitrary function f(x)f(x)f(x). We can expand f(x)f(x)f(x) in terms of the complete set of eigenfunctions of A^\hat AA^ and B^\hat BB^, and write:

f(x)=∑ncnϕn(x)f(x)=\sum_nc_n\phi_n(x)f(x)=n∑​cn​ϕn​(x)

Substitute this expansion into the last euation, then we obtain:

[A^,B^]f(x)=∑ncn(anbn−bnan)ϕn(x)=0[\hat A,\hat B]f(x)=\sum_nc_n(a_nb_n-b_na_n)\phi_n(x)=0[A^,B^]f(x)=n∑​cn​(an​bn​−bn​an​)ϕn​(x)=0

Because f(x)f(x)f(x) is arbitrary, [A^,B^]=0[\hat A,\hat B]=0[A^,B^]=0. Thus, we see that A^\hat AA^ and B^\hat BB^ commute if they have the same set of eigenfunctions.

The converse is also true; if A^\hat AA^ and B^\hat BB^ commute, then they have a mutual set of eigenfunctions.

4.8 The Probability of Obtaining a Certain Value of an Observable in a Measurement Is Given by a Fourier Coefficient

Consider a fairly arbitrary function f(x)f(x)f(x). We assume that if {ψn(x)\psi_n(x)ψn​(x)} is some orthonormal set defined over the same interval as f(x)f(x)f(x) and satisfying the same boundary conditions as f(x)f(x)f(x), then it is possible to write f(x)f(x)f(x) as:

f(x)=∑n=1∞cnψn(x)f(x)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infin}c_n\psi_n(x)f(x)=n=1∑∞​cn​ψn​(x)

A set of functions such as the ψn(x)\psi_n(x)ψn​(x) here is said to be complete if the equation holds for a suitably arbitrary function f(x)f(x)f(x). It is generally difficult to prove completeness, and in practice one usually assumes that the orthonormal set associated with some Hermitian operator is complete. Then we find:

⟨m∣f(x)⟩=cm\langle m|f(x) \rangle =c_m⟨m∣f(x)⟩=cm​

All the terms in the summation equal zero except for the one term where n=mn=mn=m.

The expansion of a function in terms of an orthonormal set is an important and useful technique in many branches of physics and chemistry. The expansion of a function in terms of an orthonormal set is called a Fourier expansion or a Fourier series. The coefficients cnc_ncn​ in the expansion are called Fourier coefficients.

Postulate 4 tells us how to calculate the average in a series of measurements:

⟨a⟩=⟨ψ(x)∣A^∣ψ(x)⟩\langle a \rangle = \langle \psi(x)|\hat A|\psi(x) \rangle⟨a⟩=⟨ψ(x)∣A^∣ψ(x)⟩

What is the probability of obtaining the particular result ana_nan​ in a single measurement? Well, we find that we can interpret ∣cn∣2|c_n|^2∣cn​∣2 as the probability of observing EnE_nEn​ when carrying out a measurement on the system, or:

probability of observing En=∣cn∣2probability\ of\ observing\ E_n = |c_n|^2probability of observing En​=∣cn​∣2

4.9 The Time Dependence of Wave Functions Is Governed by the Time-Dependent Schrödinger Equation

  • Postulate 5: The wave function or state function of a system evolves in time according to the time-dependent Schrödinger equation:

H^Ψ(x,t)=iℏ∂Ψ∂t\hat H \Psi(x,t)=i\hbar \frac {\partial \Psi}{\partial t}H^Ψ(x,t)=iℏ∂t∂Ψ​

For most systems that we shall study in this book, H^\hat HH^ does not contain time explicitly, and in this case we can apply the method of separation of variables and write:

Ψ(x,t)=ψ(x)f(t)\Psi(x,t)=\psi(x)f(t)Ψ(x,t)=ψ(x)f(t)

Ψ(x,t)=ψ(x)e−iωt\Psi(x,t)=\psi(x)e^{-i\omega t}Ψ(x,t)=ψ(x)e−iωt

It is interesting to note that the equation oscillates harmonically in time and is characteristic of wave motion. Yet the time-dependent Schrödinger equation does not have the same form as a classical wave equation. Nevertheless, the Schrödinger equation does have wavelike solutions, which is one reason why quantum mechanics is sometimes called wave mechanics.

We can use the time-dependent Schrödinger equation to derive an explicit expression for the time dependence of the average value of an operator. Start with:

⟨A⟩=∫dτΨ∗(x,t)A^(x,t)Ψ(x,t)\langle A\rangle = \int d\tau \Psi^*(x,t)\hat A(x,t)\Psi(x,t)⟨A⟩=∫dτΨ∗(x,t)A^(x,t)Ψ(x,t)

Differentiate with respect to ttt to obtain:

d⟨A⟩dt=∫dτ(iH^Ψ∗ℏ)A^Ψ+⟨∂A^∂t⟩+∫dτΨ∗A^(iH^Ψℏ)\frac {d\langle A \rangle}{dt} = \int d\tau \left(\frac {i\hat H\Psi^*}{\hbar} \right)\hat A\Psi + \langle {\frac {\partial \hat A}{\partial t}} \rangle + \int d\tau \Psi^*\hat A \left(\frac {i\hat H\Psi}{\hbar} \right)dtd⟨A⟩​=∫dτ(ℏiH^Ψ∗​)A^Ψ+⟨∂t∂A^​⟩+∫dτΨ∗A^(ℏiH^Ψ​)

Rewrite the equation:

d⟨A⟩dt=iℏ∫dτΨ∗H^A^Ψ−iℏ∫dτΨ∗A^H^Ψ+⟨∂A^∂t⟩=iℏ⟨Ψ∣[H^,A^]∣Ψ⟩+⟨∂A^∂t⟩\begin{aligned} \frac {d\langle A \rangle}{dt} &=\frac {i}{\hbar}\int d\tau \Psi^*\hat H\hat A\Psi - \frac {i}{\hbar}\int d\tau \Psi^*\hat A\hat H\Psi + \left\langle {\frac {\partial \hat A}{\partial t}} \right\rangle \\[3mm] &=\frac {i}{\hbar} \langle \Psi|[\hat H,\hat A]|\Psi \rangle+ \left\langle {\frac {\partial \hat A}{\partial t}} \right\rangle \end{aligned}dtd⟨A⟩​​=ℏi​∫dτΨ∗H^A^Ψ−ℏi​∫dτΨ∗A^H^Ψ+⟨∂t∂A^​⟩=ℏi​⟨Ψ∣[H^,A^]∣Ψ⟩+⟨∂t∂A^​⟩​

In fact, if we just undo the indicated integrations in the equation, we have the quantum-mechanical equation of motion of the operator A^\hat AA^ itself:

dA^dt=iℏ[H^,A^]+∂A^∂t\frac {d\hat A}{dt} = \frac {i}{\hbar}[\hat H,\hat A]+\frac {\partial \hat A}{\partial t}dtdA^​=ℏi​[H^,A^]+∂t∂A^​

Note that if A^\hat AA^ commutes with H^\hat HH^ if and does not depend explicitly on
time, then d⟨A^⟩/dt=0d\langle \hat A \rangle/dt=0d⟨A^⟩/dt=0, which means that ⟨A^⟩\langle \hat A\rangle⟨A^⟩ is a constant of motion, or is conserved.

4.10 Quantum Mechanics Can Describe the Two-Slit Experiment

You should be convinced by now that if a system is some superposition state or mixed state described by:

Ψ(x,t)=∑ncnψn(x)e−iEnt/ℏ\Psi(x,t)=\sum_nc_n\psi_n(x)e^{-iE_nt/\hbar}Ψ(x,t)=n∑​cn​ψn​(x)e−iEn​t/ℏ

then a measurement of the energy will yield one of the values EnE_nEn​ with a probability ∣cn∣2|c_n|^2∣cn​∣2.

Suppose we measure the energy at some time t0t_0t0​ and obtain the value E3E_3E3​. Now suppose that we are able to measure the energy immediately after t0t_0t0​, say at t0+ϵt_0+\epsilont0​+ϵ, where ϵ\epsilonϵ is vanishingly small. What value of the energy will we observe? Well, we just found it to be E3E_3E3​, and unless we are willing to allow the system to change its state essentially infinitely rapidly (which we are not), then we must observe the value E3E_3E3​ again.

We say that the wave function has “collapsed” from the superposition to the single state. For classical systems, a measurement of some property of the system does not alter the system in any significant way, but for quantum-mechanical systems, the measurement process has a profound effect.

（ 在我们观测系统之前，系统处于叠加态，但是我们一旦观测系统，系统就会坍缩为一个确定的状态。 ）

The interpretation of the measurement process that we have given here is due primarily to Bohr and Heisenberg, and is called the Copenhagen interpretation. The one entitled In Search of Schrödinger’s Cat is based upon a thought experiment proposed by Schrödinger in which a cat is in a state that is a superposition of a live cat and a dead cat, and just what such a state actually means.

（ 哥本哈根诠释实际上“没有做出诠释”，因为它只是在描述实验现象，目前也无法给“观测”下一个严谨的数学上的定义。此时，很难不让人想起Feynman的那句经典名言:“On the other hand, I think I can safely say that nobody understands quantum mechanics.” ）

At last, we summarizes our set of postulates:

总结

本章介绍了量子力学的基本公设，注意不同内容层次、不同内容深度的教材陈列的基本公设可能也会有差别。例如本书中的五大公设分别是：1.波函数公设和波恩概率诠释、2.力学量使用线性厄米算符表示、3.力学量的测量值为算符的本征值、4.力学量的期待值计算、5.波函数满足薛定谔方程随时间演化。不过，在不少其他教材中，并没有本书所说的公设4，而是全同粒子公设；还有的书中把算符对易作为基本公设之一。

另外，我省略了不少例题，实际上量子力学的学习是离不开习题训练的，多少得做一做。

entry.title: 《中级有机化学》章末总结6
entry.content:
第六章为亲核取代反应。拖了很久了。

第6章 亲核取代反应

6.1 饱和碳原子上的亲核取代反应

发生在卤代烷、醇、磺酸酯等有机化合物的饱和碳原子上亲核取代主要有两种机理：单分子亲核取代反应SN1S_N1SN​1和双分子亲核取代反应SN2S_N2SN​2。除此之外，也有分子内亲核取代反应。

SN1S_N1SN​1反应的基本机理不必赘述。SN1S_N1SN​1反应经历碳正离子中间体，碳正离子一旦形成就会涉及碳正离子的重排，形成更稳定的碳正离子。不过多数情况下，SN1S_N1SN​1反应以构型翻转产物为主，这可以从离子对理论进行解释。

只有自由的碳正离子才会以均等的概率从两个方向接受亲核试剂的进攻，其他情况下，离去基团都倾向与从离去基团背面进攻，因此主要产物为构型翻转产物。

溶剂对反应的影响取决于反应的决速步是电荷集中的、还是电荷分散的过程。

SN2S_N2SN​2反应是一步完成的协同反应，机理同样不必赘述。SN2S_N2SN​2反应中经历一个五配位的过渡态，得到中心碳原子构型翻转的产物，这种构型翻转称为Walden翻转。

由于位阻的关系，叔卤代烷不发生SN2S_N2SN​2反应，但也有例外：

本反应能发生的原因有两点：一是因为底物中两个羰基的吸电子能力很强，C−ClC-ClC−Cl键极化很强；二是因为叠氮根负离子的位阻很小。

当底物是烯丙基卤代烃、炔丙基卤代烃、苄基卤代烃时，发生SN2S_N2SN​2反应的速率显著加快。这是因为亲核试剂和离去基团带有部分负电荷，可以通过σ(C−L)/σ(C−Nu)\sigma(C-L)/\sigma(C-Nu)σ(C−L)/σ(C−Nu)和π∗(C=C)\pi^*(C=C)π∗(C=C)的相互作用而得到分散。因此，不饱和键的存在有效地降低了过渡态的势能，使反应更易发生，也就是我们常说的活化作用。

烯丙基卤代烃发生SN2S_N2SN​2反应的同时，可以发生SN2′S_N2'SN​2′反应，发生烯丙基重排。

一般情况下，亲核试剂从离去基团的同侧进攻，因为烯丙基正离子的π2\pi_2π2​轨道的两端是相位相反的，进攻C1C1C1的时候，亲核试剂从离去基团的异侧进攻；进攻C3C3C3时，亲核试剂从离去基团的同侧进攻，才满足轨道方向性的原则。

SN2S_N2SN​2和SN2′S_N2'SN​2′的竞争反应可以通过亲核试剂的结构进行控制，RRR基团增大时，易发生SN2′S_N2'SN​2′反应。

醇与二氯亚砜的反应是将醇转化为氯代物的常用方法。在二氧六环中，仲醇与二氯亚砜反应，经历两次SN2S_N2SN​2后得到构型保持产物。若在吡啶中进行反应，则只发生一次SN2S_N2SN​2反应，故得到构型翻转产物。

经典的Arbuzov反应和Gabriel反应是两个重要的例子：

亚磷酸酯和卤代烃在加热条件下生成膦酸酯的反应称为Arbuzov反应。

邻苯二甲酰亚胺的钾盐在非质子性溶剂中和空间位阻小的伯卤代烃或仲卤代烃发生亲核取代反应得到N-烷基化的邻苯二甲酰亚胺，通过酸/碱/肼处理得伯胺称为Gabriel反应。

分子内亲核取代反应用SNiS_NiSN​i表示，例如醇与二氯亚砜作用生成卤代烷的反应若在无溶剂条件下进行，反应则按照SNiS_NiSN​i反应进行：

反应中可能经过协同的四元环过渡态，或经历离子对机理，这两种情况目前仍尚处争议。

邻近基团参与（简称邻基参与，NGP）是分子内富电子性中心对缺电子性中心进行捕获的一种现象，它和分子间反应相竞争，能改变反应速率、发生骨架重构、控制反应的立体化学。

发生邻基参与的前提是富电子性中心和缺电子性中心的轨道能级要匹配、轨道之间有足够的重叠。这些满足条件的基团先发生分子内亲核取代生成环状中间体，然后再接受亲核试剂的进攻，从而加快取代反应的速率。

羧基的氧原子容易发生邻基参与，比如下面这个很经典的例子：

在该反应中，羧基负离子先发生邻基参与形成三元内酯中间体，然后亲核试剂再开环进攻，由于经历了两次SN2S_N2SN​2反应，所以中心碳原子的构型得以保持。

类似的，酯基的氧原子亦容易发生邻基参与效应，如：

这两个反应都给出反式产物，第一个反应为反式底物，立体构型上易于发生邻基参与，所以最终构型保持；第二个反应为顺式底物，难以发生邻基参与，通过SN1S_N1SN​1机理以相同的五元环氧鎓中间体完成反应。

与氧相比，硫的亲核性更强，也就更易于发生邻基参与。

氮也可以发生邻基参与，如2-氯甲基-N-乙基吡咯烷能够通过氮的邻基参与发生扩环：

具有6π电子体系的苯环是常见的邻基参与基团，苯环的邻基参与经历了一个螺环结构的苯鎓离子中间体。

苯环的这种邻基参与效应已经得到了立体化学研究结果的支持，试验结果与猜测机理相符。既然邻基参与的基团是电子给体，那么基团的富电子性越强，其邻基参与就越显著。给电子基能够稳定苯鎓离子中间体，降低过渡态势能，有效地促进邻基参与的发生：

烯烃能够提供π电子而产生邻基参与效应，反应经历一个非经典的碳正离子中间体：

在上一个例子中，具有双键的底物（Ⅰ）比底物（Ⅱ）的反应快101110^{11}1011倍。

碳碳单键也能提供电子来促进亲核取代反应的发生，如下面的例子：

三种化合物的相对反应速率为exo−A:endo−A:B=350:1:1exo-\bold A : endo-\bold A : \bold B = 350:1:1exo−A:endo−A:B=350:1:1。表明exo−Aexo-\bold Aexo−A最易发生亲核取代，endo−Aendo-\bold Aendo−A和B\bold BB的反应速率不受骨架影响。exo−Aexo-\bold Aexo−A速率很快的原因在于分子内存在σ(C1−C6)\sigma(C1-C6)σ(C1−C6)和σ∗(C2−O)\sigma^*(C2-O)σ∗(C2−O)之间的超共轭作用，能促进C−OC-OC−O键解离，形成具有对称面的非经典碳正离子中间体，因此最终会得到100%外消旋产物。

6.2 芳环上的亲核取代反应

芳烃上的卤素不能接受亲核试剂的直接进攻，因为卤素和芳环存在一定共轭，C−XC-XC−X键拥有部分双键性质，具有一定的稳定性。所以芳环上的亲核取代反应通常经过其他机理。

当芳香烃上有吸电子取代基时（EWG），亲核试剂对C−XC-XC−X键发生亲核取代反应经过加成-消除机理。

该机理的直接证据是分离得到中间体Meisenheimer盐：

吸电子基的强度会显著影响反应的速率，很容易理解 ，芳环越缺电子，那么反应就越易发生。一个具体的例子：2,4-二硝基氟苯与哌啶的亲核取代反应速率是2,4-二硝基碘苯的3300倍，虽然碘离子是更好的离去基团，但是氟的吸电子能力更强，所以反应更快。

除了常见的离去基团，氢也可以离去。例如吡啶与氨基钠反应，通过加成-消除机理生成2-氨基吡啶，该反应称为Chichibabin反应：

反应中经历氢负离子的消除，氢负离子在体系中立即反应生成氢气。

（ 这个反应的名字莫名好笑，所以我印象比较深刻，Chichibabin是一位俄罗斯化学家的名字。另外该反应与下文提及的VNS有异曲同工之妙。 ）

除了加成-消除机理外，芳香亲核取代还有消除-加成机理，这种机理会经历苯炔中间体，一般于反应过程中原位产生。

三氟甲磺酸（2-三甲硅基苯基）酯是常用的苯炔前体，它可在氟负离子的促进下生成苯炔：

除此之外，邻氨基苯甲酸衍生的重氮盐的热消除、邻氟苯基格氏试剂的消除也是产生苯炔的重要方法。

苯炔非常活泼，许多亲核试剂都能与它发生亲核加成反应，产物相当于是亲核试剂对于苯炔的插入，例如苯炔与丙二酸二乙酯的反应：

上述反应的净结果相当于苯炔对C−CC-CC−C键的插入。下面是更多的例子：

这种插入反应可以用于构建各种环，例如天然产物curvularin的合成：

除C−CC-CC−C键插入外，苯炔还可以发生C−XC-XC−X键插入或C−NC-NC−N键插入，例如苯炔对DMF的C=OC=OC=O双键插入：

在该反应中，DMF中羰基氧亲核进攻苯炔形成芳基负离子，接着通过四元环的成环开环成为亚胺盐中间体，最后水解得到最终产物。若把捕获剂换为苯甲酰腈，酰基作亲电基团，氰基负离子作亲核基团，得到如下产物：

除了上述提到的常规苯炔前体外，一般的卤代物也可以发生消除-加成反应：

对于不同的卤代物，反应性为溴苯>碘苯>氯苯>氟苯，这个顺序是离去性和吸电子诱导效应的综合结果。

在苯炔的形成和反应过程中，取代基的诱导效应都产生重要影响，由于取代基的诱导效应，炔键的形成位置和亲核试剂的加成位置都会不同。例如间甲氧基氯苯的消除-加成反应：

在消除-加成机理中，加成所产生的芳基负离子可进一步被亲电试剂捕获，完成一系列串联反应。例如天然产物dehydroaltenuene B的全合成：

当缺电子性芳香烃和带有离去基团的亲核试剂反应时，生成芳香烃上氢被亲核取代的产物，该反应则称为芳香烃间接亲核取代（vicarious nucleophilic substitution, VNS）。该反应的关键是亲核试剂上自带的离去基团的离去，这一步可以通过协同的1,2-H迁移途径或在碱性条件下的消除途径完成：

芳香亲核取代还有一种芳基碳正离子机理，这种机理较为少见，最常见的是芳基重氮盐的反应，反应属于单分子亲核取代反应。例如Balz-Schiemann反应：

这是一个向芳环上引入氟原子的有效反应。

6.3 羧酸及其衍生物的亲核取代反应

亲核试剂进攻羧酸、酰氯、酸酐、酯或酰胺的羰基碳，经历加成-消除机理后得到亲核取代产物。这也是基础有机中经典的反应，反应活性为酰氯>酸酐>酯>酰胺。

羧酸衍生物之间可以互相转化，例如各衍射物水解则得羧酸，用醇解则得酯，氨解则得酰胺。这些反应的机理本质上都相同，都是先加成，后消除的途径，根据条件不同（酸/碱催化、单分子/双分子机理、酰氧键/烷氧键断裂）可以分为八种：AAc1、BAc1、AAc2、BAc2、AAl1、BAl1、AAl2、BAl2A_{Ac}1、B_{Ac}1、A_{Ac}2、B_{Ac}2、A_{Al}1、B_{Al}1、A_{Al}2、B_{Al}2AAc​1、BAc​1、AAc​2、BAc​2、AAl​1、BAl​1、AAl​2、BAl​2。

当然以上只是排列组合的结果，实际上BAl1B_{Al}1BAl​1尚未通过实验证实，另有几种机理也极为少见。最常见的两种机理为四面体机理：AAc2A_{Ac}2AAc​2和BAc2B_{Ac}2BAc​2。

本节中许多反应都较为常见，在此不多赘述，仅讨论酰胺活化内容。

酰胺因其结构中O,C,NO,C,NO,C,N的共振，使其性质很稳定，不易发生亲核取代反应，调整胺的结构可以有效抑制酰胺的共振：

在上例中，底物四个甲基的位阻阻碍了酰胺的共振，因而使得转化活性提升。

也可以让酰胺的N端形成稳定结构来削弱酰胺的共振，例如：

最直接的方法还是利用过渡金属直接活化并切断酰胺的C−NC-NC−N键：

总结

本章为亲核取代反应，邻基参与的部分是之前了解不多的内容。

悲伤画图…

entry.title: 《物理化学》章末总结7
entry.content:
统计热力学，最不化学的一章。

第七章 统计热力学基础

（ 本节涉及大量数学运算，计算细节均省略，仅给出最终结果。 ）

7.1 概论

一切粒子都在不停地运动，每个粒子的运动都遵守力学规律。但是想用力学中的微分方程去描述系统的运动状态是不可能的，必须用统计学的方法，推求极大数目粒子运动的统计平均。人们最早是用统计的方法来研究气体的行为，现在通称为气体分子动理论，以后才发展为统计力学（statistical mechanics）。

统计力学把系统的微观性质和宏观性质联系起来，从这个角度来说，又可以称为统计热力学（statistical thermodynamics）。

根据对物质结构的某些基本假定，以及实验获得的光谱数据，可以求出物质的一些基本常数，利用这些数据可以算出配分函数（partition function），然后再求出物质的热力学性质。这就是统计热力学的基本任务。

对于简单分子，使用统计热力学得到的结果相当令人满意，但是对于大的游离分子或凝聚系统，应用统计热力学的结果还存在很大困难。

本书主要介绍Boltzmann统计，但是已经采用能量量子化的概念加以修正，再根据情况过渡到经典统计所能适用的公式。

先快速引入一些基本概念：

按照统计单位（粒子）是否可以分辨，把系统分为定位系统（localized system）和非定位系统（non-localized system）。前者的粒子可以彼此分辨，如晶体中相对固定的粒子；后者的粒子不能彼此分辨，如气体分子始终在混乱运动。

按照统计单位之间有无相互作用，把系统分为近独立粒子系统（assembly of independent particles）和非独立粒子系统（assembly of interacting particles）。前者粒子之间的相互作用可以忽略，系统总能量等于各粒子能量之和；后者粒子之间的相互作用不能忽略，是各粒子坐标的函数。

系统的热力学概率Ω\OmegaΩ是指系统在一定宏观状态下的微观状态数，满足公式S=kln⁡ΩS=k\ln\OmegaS=klnΩ.

（ 注意Ω\OmegaΩ虽然被叫做热力学概率，但是它和我们一般讨论的数学概率不同，数学概率总是落入[0,1]的区间内，而热力学概率表示的是系统的微态数，通常它是一个相当大的数字。 ）

7.2 Boltzmann统计

考虑一个系统有NNN个可以区分的分子，分子间的作用不计，分子的能级是量子化的，同时分子的运动会让它们互相交换能量，所以NNN个分子有不同的分布方式。

不过无论哪一种分布方式都需要满足如下两个条件：

∑iNi=N∑iNiϵi=U\sum_iN_i=N \\[3mm] \sum_iN_i\epsilon_i=Ui∑​Ni​=Ni∑​Ni​ϵi​=U

此时需要考虑如何求解Ω\OmegaΩ，Boltzmann认为在一系列分布方式中，有最大的一项tmt_mtm​可以近似代表Ω\OmegaΩ，这个假定是合理的，我们会在下文分析其合理性。

结合上述条件，通过一系列数学计算，我们就能得到微观状态数最多的一种分布，称为最概然分布（most probable distribution）：

Ni∗=eα+βϵiN_i^*=e^{\alpha+\beta\epsilon_i}Ni∗​=eα+βϵi​

上式中还包含两个待定因子α,β\alpha,\betaα,β，需要进一步计算。求出因子后就能得到最概然分布的形式。

Ni∗=Ne−ϵi/kBT∑e−ϵi/kBTN_i^*=N\frac {e^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT}}{\sum e^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT}}Ni∗​=N∑e−ϵi​/kB​Te−ϵi​/kB​T​

我们还能获得定位系统的熵和Helmholtz自由能的表达式：

S=kBNln⁡∑e−ϵi/kBT+UTS=k_BN\ln\sum e^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT}+\frac UTS=kB​Nln∑e−ϵi​/kB​T+TU​

A=−NkBTln⁡∑ie−ϵi/kBTA=-Nk_BT\ln\sum_ie^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT}A=−NkB​Tlni∑​e−ϵi​/kB​T

注意到ϵi\epsilon_iϵi​与体积有关，所以上式中AAA是(T,V,N)(T,V,N)(T,V,N)的函数，即AAA是特性函数。

在量子力学中，我们把该能级可能有的微观状态数称为该能级的简并度（degeneracy），用gig_igi​表示。实际上，在考虑定位系统时，简并度会影响分布的微观状态数，通过计算可得：

Ni∗=Ngie−ϵi/kBT∑igie−ϵi/kBTS定位=kBNln⁡∑igie−ϵi/kBT+UTA定位=−NkBTln⁡∑igie−ϵi/kBTN_i^* = N\frac {g_ie^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT}}{\sum_ig_ie^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT}} \\[3mm] S_{定位}=k_BN\ln\sum_ig_ie^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT}+\frac UT \\[3mm] A_{定位}=-Nk_BT\ln\sum_ig_ie^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT}Ni∗​=N∑i​gi​e−ϵi​/kB​Tgi​e−ϵi​/kB​T​S定位​=kB​Nlni∑​gi​e−ϵi​/kB​T+TU​A定位​=−NkB​Tlni∑​gi​e−ϵi​/kB​T

对于非定位系统，我们需要对上述结果做一些修正：

Ni∗=Ngie−ϵi/kBT∑igie−ϵi/kBTS非定位=kBln⁡(∑igie−ϵi/kBT)NN!+UTA非定位=−kBTln⁡(∑igie−ϵi/kBT)NN!N_i^* = N\frac {g_ie^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT}}{\sum_ig_ie^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT}} \\[3mm] S_{非定位}=k_B\ln \frac {\left(\sum_ig_ie^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT} \right)^N}{N!}+\frac UT \\[3mm] A_{非定位}=-k_BT \ln\frac {\left(\sum_ig_ie^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT} \right)^N}{N!}Ni∗​=N∑i​gi​e−ϵi​/kB​Tgi​e−ϵi​/kB​T​S非定位​=kB​lnN!(∑i​gi​e−ϵi​/kB​T)N​+TU​A非定位​=−kB​TlnN!(∑i​gi​e−ϵi​/kB​T)N​

无论定位或非定位系统，最概然分布的公式是一样的，但在SSS和AAA的表示式中却不尽相同，相差一些常数项，而这些常数项在计算热力学函数的变化值时可以相互消去。

Boltzmann公式常转化为不同形式：

Ni∗Nj∗=gie−ϵi/kBTgje−ϵj/kBT\frac {N_i^*}{N_j^*}=\frac {g_ie^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT}}{g_je^{-\epsilon_j/k_BT}}Nj∗​Ni∗​​=gj​e−ϵj​/kB​Tgi​e−ϵi​/kB​T​

假定最低能级为ϵ0\epsilon_0ϵ0​，在该能级上的粒子数为N0N_0N0​，则：

Ni=N0e−Δϵi/kBTN_i=N_0e^{-\Delta\epsilon_i/k_BT}Ni​=N0​e−Δϵi​/kB​T

在推导Boltzmann公式时，曾作以下假定：

  • 在所有的分布方式中，有一种分布方式热力学概率最大，称为最概然分布。
  • 最概然分布的状态数最多，基本上可以用它代替总的微观状态，也就是说最概然分布实质上可以代表一切分布，最概然分布实际上也就是平衡分布。

我们在这里加以说明。

数学推导

根据计算可得：

ln⁡(tm+δttm)=−12∑t(δNi)2Ni∗\ln \left(\frac {t_m+\delta t}{t_m} \right)=-\frac 12\sum_t\frac {(\delta N_i)^2}{N_i^*}ln(tm​tm​+δt​)=−21​t∑​Ni∗​(δNi​)2​

上式表明，不论偏差δNi\delta N_iδNi​是正是负，等号右侧总是负值，所以tmt_mtm​总是大于(tm+δt)(t_m+\delta t)(tm​+δt)。不妨假设Ni∗=3×1019N_i^*=3\times10^{19}Ni∗​=3×1019，并且令偏移等于1%（δNi/Ni∗=0.01\delta N_i/N_i^*=0.01δNi​/Ni∗​=0.01），则可以计算出：

tm+δttm=exp⁡(−3×1015)\frac {t_m+\delta t}{t_m}=\exp(-3\times10^{15})tm​tm​+δt​=exp(−3×1015)

据此可发现偏移量是极其小的，反过来就证明了最概然分布的概率最大。

进行计算和化简近似后还可以得到：

ln⁡tm≤ln⁡Ω≤ln⁡tm+ln⁡N\ln t_m \le \ln\Omega \le \ln t_m+\ln Nlntm​≤lnΩ≤lntm​+lnN

假设N≈1024N \approx 10^{24}N≈1024，ln⁡tm\ln t_mlntm​的数量级在102310^{23}1023左右，而ln⁡N=55.262\ln N=55.262lnN=55.262，所以ln⁡N\ln NlnN项完全可以忽略，因此ln⁡tm=ln⁡Ω\ln t_m = \ln \Omegalntm​=lnΩ。

可以发现当NNN足够大时，最概然分布足以代表系统的一切分布。


7.3 Bose-Einstein统计和Fermi-Dirac统计

根据量子力学原理，已知基本粒子和由奇数个基本粒子组成的原子和分子必须遵循Pauli不相容原理，即每一个量子状态最多只能容纳一个粒子。但对光子以及由偶数个基本粒子组成的原子和分子则不受Pauli不相容原理的制约，即每个量子状态所能容纳的粒子数没有限制。

这两类粒子适用的统计方法是不同的，对于前者组成的等同粒子系统服从Fermi-Dirac统计，对于后者组成的等同粒子系统则服从Bose-Einstein统计。

Bose−Einstein:Ni=gie−α−βϵi−1或giNi=e−α−βϵi−1Bose-Einstein: \\[3mm] N_i=\frac {g_i}{e^{-\alpha-\beta\epsilon_i}-1} \quad 或 \quad \frac {g_i}{N_i}=e^{-\alpha-\beta\epsilon_i}-1Bose−Einstein:Ni​=e−α−βϵi​−1gi​​或Ni​gi​​=e−α−βϵi​−1

Fermi−Dirac:Ni=gie−α−βϵi+1或giNi=e−α−βϵi+1Fermi-Dirac: \\[3mm] N_i=\frac {g_i}{e^{-\alpha-\beta\epsilon_i}+1} \quad 或 \quad \frac {g_i}{N_i}=e^{-\alpha-\beta\epsilon_i}+1Fermi−Dirac:Ni​=e−α−βϵi​+1gi​​或Ni​gi​​=e−α−βϵi​+1

这两种统计方法都是建立在量子力学的基础之上，因此通称量子统计。与Boltzmann统计的公式比较一下不难发现，它们只差了一个±1\pm1±1，由于gi≫Nig_i \gg N_igi​≫Ni​，所以两种统计方法在温度不太低或压力不太高时很容易还原到Boltzmann统计。

本书只讨论Boltzmann统计。

7.4 配分函数

已知最概然分布公式：

Ni=Ngie−ϵi/kBT∑igie−ϵi/kBTN_i = N\frac {g_ie^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT}}{\sum_ig_ie^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT}}Ni​=N∑i​gi​e−ϵi​/kB​Tgi​e−ϵi​/kB​T​

令分母：

∑igie−ϵi/kBT≡q\sum_ig_ie^{-\epsilon_i/k_BT} \equiv qi∑​gi​e−ϵi​/kB​T≡q

qqq称为粒子的配分函数（partition function），配分函数是对系统中一个粒子的所有可能状态的Boltzmann因子求和。

统计热力学的最重要的任务之一就是通过配分函数来计算系统的热力学函数。因此配分函数可以看作是联系微观和宏观的桥梁。

A定位=−kBTln⁡qNS定位=NkB[∂∂T(Tln⁡q)]V,N=NkBln⁡q+NkBT(∂ln⁡q∂T)V,NU定位=NkBT2(∂ln⁡q∂T)V,NG定位=A+pV=−kBTln⁡qN+NkBTV(∂ln⁡q∂V)T,NH定位=U+pV=NkBT2(∂ln⁡q∂T)V,N+NkBTV(∂ln⁡q∂T)T,NCV,定位=∂∂T[NkBT2(∂ln⁡q∂T)V,N]VA_{定位}=-k_BT\ln q^N \\[3mm]S_{定位}=Nk_B \left[\frac {\partial}{\partial T}(T\ln q) \right]_{V,N}=Nk_B\ln q+Nk_BT \left(\frac {\partial \ln q}{\partial T} \right)_{V,N} \\[3mm]U_{定位}=Nk_BT^2 \left(\frac {\partial \ln q}{\partial T} \right)_{V,N} \\[3mm]G_{定位}=A+pV=-k_BT\ln q^N+Nk_BTV \left(\frac {\partial \ln q}{\partial V} \right)_{T,N} \\[3mm]H_{定位}=U+pV=Nk_BT^2 \left(\frac {\partial \ln q}{\partial T} \right)_{V,N}+Nk_BTV \left(\frac {\partial \ln q}{\partial T} \right)_{T,N} \\[3mm]C_{V,定位}=\frac {\partial}{\partial T} \left[Nk_BT^2 \left(\frac {\partial \ln q}{\partial T} \right)_{V,N} \right]_{V}A定位​=−kB​TlnqNS定位​=NkB​[∂T∂​(Tlnq)]V,N​=NkB​lnq+NkB​T(∂T∂lnq​)V,N​U定位​=NkB​T2(∂T∂lnq​)V,N​G定位​=A+pV=−kB​TlnqN+NkB​TV(∂V∂lnq​)T,N​H定位​=U+pV=NkB​T2(∂T∂lnq​)V,N​+NkB​TV(∂T∂lnq​)T,N​CV,定位​=∂T∂​[NkB​T2(∂T∂lnq​)V,N​]V​

接着我们来进行配分函数的分离。一个分子的能量可以认为是分子整体运动的能量即平动能（ϵt\epsilon_tϵt​）以及分子内部的转动能（ϵr\epsilon_rϵr​），振动能（ϵv\epsilon_vϵv​），电子运动的能量（ϵe\epsilon_eϵe​）和核运动的能量（ϵn\epsilon_nϵn​）。分子处于某能级的能量可以看作各种能量之和。

这几个能级的大小次序是：

ϵn>ϵe>ϵv>ϵr>ϵt\epsilon_n>\epsilon_e>\epsilon_v>\epsilon_r>\epsilon_tϵn​>ϵe​>ϵv​>ϵr​>ϵt​

可以推得：

q=qt⋅qr⋅qv⋅qe⋅qnq=q_t\cdot q_r \cdot q_v \cdot q_e \cdot q_nq=qt​⋅qr​⋅qv​⋅qe​⋅qn​

7.5 各配分函数的求法及其对热力学函数的贡献

原子核配分函数可以写作（近似后结果）：

qn=gn,0 exp⁡(−ϵn,0kBT)q_n=g_{n,0}\,\exp \left(-\frac {\epsilon_{n,0}}{k_BT} \right)qn​=gn,0​exp(−kB​Tϵn,0​​)

除了核反应外，通常的化学反应过程中，原子核总是处于基态，若将核基态能量选作零，则：

qn=gn,0q_n=g_{n,0}qn​=gn,0​

核能级的简并度来源自原子核的自旋，但是自旋方向不同的各态之间没有显著能量差别，只有在超精细结构中才能看出。

电子配分函数可以写作（近似后结果，且规定最低能态能量为零）：

qe=ge,0q_e=g_{e,0}qe​=ge,0​

电子绕核运动的简并度来源自电子的总动量矩，与核能级简并度类似。

核配分函数与电子配分函数对于U,H,CVU,H,C_VU,H,CV​的贡献均为零，而对A,G,SA,G,SA,G,S会产生影响。

注意到有些原子中，电子的基态和第一激发态之间的间隔不是很大，此时需要考虑qeq_eqe​表达式的第二项，相应地它对各种热力学函数的贡献也就无法忽略。

平动配分函数可以写作：

qt=∑igi,t exp⁡(−ϵi,tkBT)q_t=\sum_ig_{i,t}\,\exp \left(-\frac {\epsilon_{i,t}}{k_BT} \right)qt​=i∑​gi,t​exp(−kB​Tϵi,t​​)

根据势箱模型，可以从波动方程求出平动能的能量ϵi,t\epsilon_{i,t}ϵi,t​，这部分在一般的结构化学或量子化学课程中都会学习。因此给出进一步的结果：

qt=(2πmkBTh2)3/2⋅Vq_t=\left(\frac {2\pi mk_BT}{h^2} \right)^{3/2} \cdot Vqt​=(h22πmkB​T​)3/2⋅V

平动配分函数对热力学函数的贡献如下：

At=−NkBTln⁡[(2πmkBTh2)3/2V]+NkBTln⁡N−NkBTSt=NkB(ln⁡qtN+52)A_t=-Nk_BT\ln \left[\left(\frac {2\pi mk_BT}{h^2} \right)^{3/2} V\right]+Nk_BT\ln N-Nk_BT \\[3mm]S_t=Nk_B\left(\ln\frac {q_t}{N}+\frac 52 \right)At​=−NkB​Tln[(h22πmkB​T​)3/2V]+NkB​TlnN−NkB​TSt​=NkB​(lnNqt​​+25​)

这个公式称为Sackur-Tetrode公式，可用来计算理想气体的平动熵。

对于双原子分子，转动配分函数可以写作（忽略转动和振动的相互作用）：

qr=8π2IkBTσh2=TΘrσq_r=\frac {8\pi^2Ik_BT}{\sigma h^2}=\frac {T}{\Theta_r\sigma}qr​=σh28π2IkB​T​=Θr​σT​

式中σ\sigmaσ称为对称数（symmetry number），它是分子经过刚性转动一周后，所产生的不可分辨的几何位置数。对于同核双原子分子，σ=2\sigma=2σ=2。Θr\Theta_rΘr​称为转动特征温度，因为其单位为KKK。

（ 对称数也就是对称轴的最高轴次，或者说是主轴轴次。 ）

对于转动特征温度较高的分子，经常需考虑激发态的量子态。

对于非线性多原子分子，可以证明其转动配分函数为：

qr=8π2(2πkBT)3/2σh3⋅(Ix⋅Iy⋅Iz)1/2q_r=\frac {8\pi^2(2\pi k_BT)^{3/2}}{\sigma h^3}\cdot (I_x\cdot I_y \cdot I_z)^{1/2}qr​=σh38π2(2πkB​T)3/2​⋅(Ix​⋅Iy​⋅Iz​)1/2

对于双原子分子，它的振动配分函数可以写作（近似后结果）：

qv′=11−e−hν/kBTq_v'=\frac 1{1-e^{-h\nu/k_BT}}qv′​=1−e−hν/kB​T1​

qv′q_v'qv′​是把振动基态能量作为零时的振动配分函数。分子基态的振动能量为ϵv,0=12hν\epsilon_{v,0}=\frac 12h\nuϵv,0​=21​hν，称为零点振动能（zero point energy）。

对于多原子分子，需要考虑分子的自由度，描述一个分子质心在空间的位置需要三个坐标参数，描述分子骨架的空间取向需要三个角度参数（线性分子只需两个），考虑分子中的nnn的原子总的自由度为3n3n3n，则振动自由度为3n−3−33n-3-33n−3−3（线性分子振动自由度则为3n−3−23n-3-23n−3−2）。

有了自由度，就可以给出振动配分函数，对于非线形多原子分子：

qv=∏i=13n−6e−hνi/2kBT1−e−hνi/kBTq_v=\prod_{i=1}^{3n-6}\frac {e^{-h\nu_i/2k_BT}}{1-e^{-h\nu_i/k_BT}}qv​=i=1∏3n−6​1−e−hνi​/kB​Te−hνi​/2kB​T​

7.6 晶体的热容问题

经典理论认为，晶体中的原子在晶格上做简谐振动，按照能量均分定理，推出其摩尔热容为：

CV,m=(∂U∂T)V=3R=24.94J⋅mol−1⋅K−1C_{V,m}=\left(\frac {\partial U}{\partial T} \right)_V=3R=24.94J\cdot mol^{-1}\cdot K^{-1}CV,m​=(∂T∂U​)V​=3R=24.94J⋅mol−1⋅K−1

这是一个经验定律，称为Dulong-Petit定律，即固体物质的摩尔热容大致相等。

但是实际情况不是这样，当温度降低，摩尔热容逐渐减小，且不同单质的摩尔热容随温度变化率也不相同。经典理论无法解释。

1907年，Einstein用量子论来解释晶体的热容，对这个问题给出了一个初步的解释。但是Einstein的结果与实验曲线不完全相合，这说明他的假设中存在些许问题。

Debye对Einstein理论提出了修正，并得到了令人满意的结果。当温度趋于零时：

CV,m=1943(TΘD)3J⋅mol−1⋅K−1=constant×T3\begin{aligned} C_{V,m} &=1943 \left(\frac {T}{\Theta_D} \right)^3 J\cdot mol^{-1} \cdot K^{-1} \\[3mm] &=constant \times T^3 \end{aligned}CV,m​​=1943(ΘD​T​)3J⋅mol−1⋅K−1=constant×T3​

即T3T^3T3定律，ΘD\Theta_DΘD​称为Debye温度，该公式的计算值与实验值相一致，说明了Debye处理问题的正确性。

7.7 分子的全配分函数

将上述讨论的几种配分函数合并，就得到分子的全配分函数：

q总=qn⋅qe⋅qt⋅qr⋅qvq_总=q_n \cdot q_e \cdot q_t \cdot q_r \cdot q_vq总​=qn​⋅qe​⋅qt​⋅qr​⋅qv​

对于单原子分子：

q总=[gn,0exp⁡(−ϵn,0kBT)]⋅[ge,0exp⁡(−ϵe,0kBT)]⋅[(2πmkBT)3/2h3V]q_总= \left[g_{n,0}\exp \left(-\frac {\epsilon_{n,0}}{k_BT} \right)\right]\cdot \left[g_{e,0}\exp \left(-\frac {\epsilon_{e,0}}{k_BT}\right)\right] \cdot \left[\frac {(2\pi mk_BT)^{3/2}}{h^3}V \right]q总​=[gn,0​exp(−kB​Tϵn,0​​)]⋅[ge,0​exp(−kB​Tϵe,0​​)]⋅[h3(2πmkB​T)3/2​V]

对于双原子分子：
